12997.text: Who is angry: The same words for God and people; some words kept for God (part A). In restraint God sets himself against a man: "for I am God and not a man".

12998.text: What sets it off: God and people both: "when the Lord heard it, his anger was kindled"; "As soon as his master heard the words"; a sight: "when Haman saw Mordecai"; a refusal: "But Queen Vashti refused to come"; "Behold, I thought that he would surely come out to me"; news and alarm: "news from the east and the north shall alarm him, and he shall go out with great fury".

12999.text: Whether what sets it off is true: Potiphar's anger rises on his wife's report, untested; the officials rage at Jeremiah's "It is a lie; I am not deserting"; the disciples' "Why this waste?" is answered "she has done a beautiful thing to me".

13000.text: For whom, and against whom the bond is defended: For the widow and fatherless: "my wrath will burn"; jealous wrath against Jerusalem ("the blood of wrath and jealousy") and for Zion ("I am jealous for her with great wrath"); Jesus "was indignant" for the children.

13001.text: What it is joined with in the verse: Jealousy (Deu 6:15); grief: Jonathan "was grieved for David", Jesus "looked around at them with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart"; the Spirit (1Sa 11:6); "the anger and envy that you showed because of your hatred" (Eze 35:11); fear: "he shall be afraid and withdraw, and shall turn back and be enraged"; compassion set against it (Hos 11:8–9).

13002.text: Time: God's: "For his anger is but for a moment"; "in a very little while my fury will come to an end"; "the wrath of God is finished"; "the wrath of God remains on him". A man's: Edom "kept his wrath forever"; "until your brother's anger turns away from you, and he forgets"; "do not let the sun go down on your anger".

13003.text: The answer it meets: "A soft answer turns away wrath"; "A gift in secret averts anger"; Moses' plea; "when he humbled himself the wrath of the Lord turned from him"; Aaron's reason, "And when Moses heard that, he approved"; Naaman's servants; "His father came out and entreated him"; Jesus called the ten; Gamaliel's counsel. Or none: "I sought for a man … but I found none"; "I looked, but there was no one to help".

13004.text: The stated reason for God's restraint: "being compassionate"; "I acted for the sake of my name, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations"; "had I not feared provocation by the enemy"; "for the spirit would grow faint before me"; "for I am merciful"; "They have humbled themselves. I will not destroy them".

13005.text: Power: The ruler's anger is followed at once by a command: custody, a decree, destruction, killing. "A king's wrath is like the growling of a lion".

13006.text: The one who carries it out: "Woe to Assyria, the rod of my anger … but it is in his heart to destroy"; "you showed them no mercy"; "while I was angry but a little, they furthered the disaster"; "you have killed them in a rage that has reached up to heaven"; Saul judged for not carrying it out.

13007.text: One and many: "shall one man sin, and will you be angry with all the congregation?"; Achan's act and the people's breach; Hezekiah's proud heart and "wrath came upon him and Judah and Jerusalem".

13008.text: What the angry person does with it: Nehemiah: "I took counsel with myself"; Absalom "spoke to Amnon neither good nor bad"; Jacob's sons answered "deceitfully"; Samuel "cried to the Lord all night"; David "was afraid of the Lord that day"; Sanballat and Tobiah "plotted together"; Ahab "lay down on his bed and turned away his face"; Paul "reasoned in the synagogue".

13009.text: Who speaks to it: God asks: "Why are you angry, and why has your face fallen?"; "Do you do well to be angry?"; Joseph: "do not be distressed or angry with yourselves"; "Fret not yourself"; "Be angry and do not sin".

13010.text: Where it sits in the person: "his anger burned within him"; "in the heat of my spirit"; "my spirit drinks their poison"; "my eye is wasted from grief; my soul and my body also"; "anger lodges in the heart of fools"; "his spirit was provoked within him"; "his heart rages against the Lord".

13011.text: The same words in different settings: One storm sentence among the false prophets and among the promises (Jer 23:19 = 30:23); the Exodus "a mighty hand and an outstretched arm" with "wrath poured out" added, aimed at Israel; provocation as threat and as a question inside a lament ("Why have they provoked me to anger with their carved images"); kaʿas as what "kills the fool" and as the "Sorrow" that "is better than laughter".

13012.text: The same phrase, the speaker's purpose: "slow to anger": God's proclaimed name, Moses' plea, Joel's call to return, Nahum's warning, Jonah's complaint, the wise man's virtue.

13013.text: One root, different things: ʾaph: "pressing the nose produces blood, and pressing anger produces strife"; ḥēmāh: wrath, "the venom of asps", "the heat of wine"; ʿebrāh: wrath and "arrogant pride"; zāʿam: anger and "How can I denounce"; zāʿap̄: Uzziah's anger and "Why are your faces downcast today?"; ʿāšan: "Mount Sinai was wrapped in smoke" and "Why does your anger smoke"; kāʿas: provoking God and Hannah's "vexation"; thymos: God's "wrath" and Babylon's "passion"; paroxysmos: "a sharp disagreement" and "stir up one another to love".

13014.text: Who else is in the scene: an intercessor (Exo 32:11); an onlooker whose gladness bears on it (Pro 24:18); a prophet sent with a question (2Ch 25:15); an angel who asks "how long" (Zec 1:12); destroying angels (Psa 78:49); the created world (Jer 7:20); brothers who "exhort one another every day" (Heb 3:13); the authority, "an avenger who carries out God's wrath" (Rom 13:4).

13015.text: Correction with or without the anger: "I myself will discipline you sevenfold for your sins", "in fury"; against it: "rebuke me not in your anger, nor discipline me in your wrath"; "Correct me, O Lord, but in justice; not in your anger".

13016.text: The measure: "to increase still more the fierce anger of the Lord"; "Ahab did more to provoke the Lord … than all the kings"; "storing up wrath for yourself"; "so as always to fill up the measure of their sins" is the setting of "wrath has come upon them at last".

13017.text: What follows a person's anger is where the cases differ (v2, U1 §37): the face falls: "So Cain was very angry, and his face fell"; speech: "I must speak, that I may find relief"; counsel: "I took counsel with myself"; fear: "And David was afraid of the Lord that day"; mercy: "Not a man shall be put to death this day".

13019.text: The leader bears it differently from the people (v2, U2 §65 point 4): Moses: "But the Lord was angry with me because of you"; Aaron "stood between the dead and the living"; David: "let your hand be against me and against my father's house"; and none found: "I sought for a man among them who should build up the wall and stand in the breach before me for the land … but I found none".

13020.text: Prayer and anger meet (v2, U2 §65 points 5 and 7): "how long will you be angry with your people's prayers?"; "you have wrapped yourself with a cloud so that no prayer can pass through"; "As for you, do not pray for this people"; "There is no one who calls upon your name"; "As I called, and they would not hear, so they called, and I would not hear"; "we do not present our pleas before you because of our righteousness, but because of your great mercy".

13021.text: God's anger leads to giving over: "and he gave them over to plunderers"; "he gave them into the hand of the nations".

13022.text: God's anger leads to the land and the harvest: "he will shut up the heavens, so that there will be no rain"; "They shall be ashamed of their harvests because of the fierce anger of the Lord".

13023.text: God's anger leads to presence withdrawn; no hearing: "and he departed. When the cloud removed from over the tent"; "though they cry in my ears with a loud voice, I will not hear them"; "As I called, and they would not hear, so they called, and I would not hear".

13024.text: God's anger leads to people turning on each other: "the people are like fuel for the fire; no one spares another".

13025.text: God's anger leads to ordinary joy, grief and courage stopped: "Let not the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn, for wrath is upon all their multitude"; "none goes to battle".

13026.text: God's anger leads to terror: "terrify them in his fury"; "The Assyrians will be terror-stricken at the voice of the Lord".

13027.text: God's anger leads to knowing; understanding later; not taken to heart: "And they shall know that I am the Lord"; "In the latter days you will understand it clearly"; "it burned him up, but he did not take it to heart".

13029.text: God's anger leads to calm, after: "I will be calm and will no more be angry".

13030.text: God's anger leads to comfort, healing, gathering, after: "your anger turned away, that you might comfort me"; "I will heal their apostasy; I will love them freely, for my anger has turned from them"; "I will gather them … and I will make them dwell in safety".

13031.text: God's anger leads to borne in the body and in company: "There is no soundness in my flesh"; "I eat ashes like bread and mingle tears with my drink"; "You have caused my companions to shun me"; "I sat alone, because your hand was upon me".

13032.text: God's anger leads to fear moving the intercessor: "For I was afraid of the anger and hot displeasure … But the Lord listened to me that time also".

13034.text: God's anger leads to the heart's joy for those it acts for: "You shall see, and your heart shall rejoice … he shall show his indignation against his enemies".

13035.text: A person's anger leads to an act at once, with the hand: Moses "threw the tablets out of his hands and broke them"; Balaam "struck the donkey with his staff"; Bigthan and Teresh "sought to lay hands on King Ahasuerus".

13036.text: A person's anger leads to a command, where the angry one has power: "and he put them in custody"; "commanded that all the wise men of Babylon be destroyed"; Herod "sent and killed all the male children in Bethlehem".

13037.text: A person's anger leads to killing: "For in their anger they killed men"; Cain "rose up against his brother Abel and killed him" follows "Why are you angry"; at Stephen, "they cried out with a loud voice and stopped their ears and rushed together at him".

13038.text: A person's anger leads to a face that falls; an eye that watches; a plot: "and his face fell"; "And Saul eyed David from that day on"; "And they all plotted together".

13039.text: A person's anger leads to strife: "A hot-tempered man stirs up strife"; "pressing anger produces strife"; "one given to anger causes much transgression".

13040.text: A person's anger leads to folly, evil, a snare: "A man of quick temper acts foolishly"; "Fret not yourself; it tends only to evil"; "lest you learn his ways and entangle yourself in a snare".

13041.text: A person's anger leads to withdrawal into the body: Hannah "wept and would not eat"; Ahab "lay down on his bed and turned away his face and would eat no food"; Jonathan "ate no food the second day of the month".

13042.text: A person's anger leads to fear; prayer: "And David was afraid of the Lord that day"; "And Samuel was angry, and he cried to the Lord all night".

13044.text: A person's anger leads to staying outside: "But he was angry and refused to go in".

13048.text: A person's anger leads to an opening for the devil: "do not let the sun go down on your anger, and give no opportunity to the devil".

13049.text: A person's anger leads to not the righteousness of God; judgment: "for the anger of man does not produce the righteousness of God"; "everyone who is angry with his brother will be liable to judgment".

13051.text: A person's anger leads to leprosy in the act: "when he became angry with the priests, leprosy broke out on his forehead".

13052.text: The same outcome is named on both sides: terror or fear (Psa 2:5; 2Sa 6:9), shame (Jer 12:13; Isa 45:24), and the body (Psa 38:3; 1Ki 21:4); no verse draws the parallel.

13053.text: A person responds to God's anger by plead: "Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak" (Gen 18:30).

13054.text: A person responds to God's anger by humble oneself, turn the heart: "when he humbled himself the wrath of the Lord turned from him" (2Ch 12:12).

13055.text: A person responds to God's anger by act to remove the cause: "Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with the Lord … in order that his fierce anger may turn away from us" (2Ch 29:10).

13056.text: A person responds to God's anger by read the ruin: "Why has the Lord done thus to this land? What caused the heat of this great anger?" (Deu 29:24).

13058.text: A person responds to God's anger by refuse the warning: "they kept mocking the messengers of God … until the wrath of the Lord rose against his people, until there was no remedy" (2Ch 36:16).

13059.text: A person responds to God's anger by ask for correction without anger: "Correct me, O Lord, but in justice; not in your anger" (Jer 10:24).

13060.text: A person responds to God's anger by fear being cast off: "Turn not your servant away in anger" (Psa 27:9).

13061.text: A person responds to God's anger by ask "how long?" as a people: "How long, O Lord? Will you be angry forever?" (Psa 79:5).

13063.text: A person responds to God's anger by take it into a view of the whole of life: "For all our days pass away under your wrath" (Psa 90:9).

13064.text: A person responds to God's anger by shelter while it passes: "hide yourselves for a little while until the fury has passed by" (Isa 26:20).

13065.text: A person responds to God's anger by hold false peace: "surely his anger has turned from me" (Jer 2:35).

13066.text: A person responds to God's anger by mourn: "For this put on sackcloth, lament and wail" (Jer 4:8).

13067.text: A person responds to God's anger by fail to take it to heart: "it burned him up, but he did not take it to heart" (Isa 42:25).

13068.text: A person responds to God's anger by know: "And they shall know that I am the Lord" (Eze 5:13).

13069.text: A person responds to God's anger by return without a guarantee: "Who knows? God may turn and relent" (Jon 3:9).

13070.text: A person responds to God's anger by bear it willingly because of one's sin: "I will bear the indignation of the Lord because I have sinned against him" (Mic 7:9).

13071.text: A person responds to God's anger by renounce vengeance and leave it to God: "never avenge yourselves, but leave it to the wrath of God" (Rom 12:19).

13072.text: A person responds to God's anger by put off what the wrath comes on: "But now you must put them all away: anger, wrath, malice, slander, and obscene talk from your mouth" (Col 3:8).

13074.text: A person responds to God's anger by speak of it as a wrath one is delivered from: "Jesus who delivers us from the wrath to come" (1Th 1:10).

13080.text: Compassion named beside "no remedy": "because he had compassion on his people and on his dwelling place"; "until there was no remedy".

13089.text: The anger that imprisons also places: "But the Lord was with Joseph" (Joseph in prison after Potiphar's anger; the officers Pharaoh imprisoned in anger later bring about his release, Gen 41:9–13).

13090.text: Source not named: "there came great wrath against Israel" (2Ki 3:27); held.

13091.text: The friends' explanations of suffering by God's anger (Eliphaz, Zophar, Elihu) are a named speaker's statement, not Scripture's own, under God's verdict "you have not spoken of me what is right" (Job 42:7); Job's "my adversary" (Job 16:9) is held beside the same verdict, unreconciled.

13092.text: Sequence in Gen 4:4–8: regard withheld → anger → face fallen → God reads the face and asks → sin at the door, "rule over it" → killing.

13093.text: Sequence in Gen 27:41–45: the blessing lost → hatred → murder planned in his heart (ESV "said to himself"; Hebrew in his heart), comforting himself → flight → waiting until the anger "turns away" and he "forgets".

13094.text: Sequence in Gen 30:1–3: seeing barrenness → envy → an impossible demand → anger naming God as the only one who could meet it → a workaround.

13095.text: Sequence in Gen 44:18–45:8: Judah's plea against anger → Joseph weeps → "dismayed" → "do not be … angry with yourselves" → reframing: "not you … but God".

13096.text: Sequence in Num 22:27–30: the donkey stops → anger → striking → the donkey speaks → "you have made a fool of me" (the anger's reason) → admission ("No").

13097.text: Sequence in 1Sa 1:6–18: provoked year by year → weeping, not eating → heart named by husband → "deeply distressed" (Hebrew bitter of soul) → heart-prayer, lips only → misread as drunk → self-explanation ("vexation") → blessing → eats, face no longer sad.

13098.text: Sequence in 1Sa 11:5–13: hearing → Spirit → anger → act → dread spreads → victory → mercy: "not a man shall be put to death".

13099.text: Sequence in 1Sa 18:7–11: a song heard → anger → reckoning ("what more can he have but the kingdom?") → watching ("eyed") → harmful spirit → spear.

13100.text: Sequence in 1Sa 20:30–34: anger at the son → insult → the spear at the son → the son knows → the son's anger + grief → fasting.

13101.text: Sequence in 2Sa 6:7–10 = 1Ch 13:10–13: God strikes Uzzah → David angry at God → David afraid of God → avoidance (the ark set aside).

13102.text: Sequence in 2Sa 12:1–7: a parable heard → anger → verdict ("deserves to die") → "You are the man!".

13103.text: Sequence in 2Sa 13:20–39: "do not take this to heart" → the king very angry, no act → the brother's hatred waits two years → killing → the king's spirit longs for the killer.

13104.text: Sequence in 1Ki 20:42–21:7: verdict on his life → sullen → refused → sullen, bed, face turned, no food → another names the spirit → the heart offered a crime as comfort.

13105.text: Sequence in 2Ki 5:11–14: expectation ("I thought") → anger → rage, going away → servants' persuasion → obedience → flesh restored.

13106.text: Sequence in 2Ch 16:9–12: diagnosis of a failed heart → rage at the seer → cruelty → disease → not seeking the Lord.

13107.text: Sequence in 2Ch 26:16–21: strength → "he grew proud" (Hebrew his heart was lifted up) → trespass → withstood → anger → leprosy in the act.

13108.text: Sequence in Neh 5:5–9: an outcry heard → anger → "I took counsel with myself" (Hebrew my heart took counsel) → charges → public assembly.

13109.text: Sequence in Est 1:10–2:1: merry heart → refusal → rage "within him" (Est 1:12) → counsel ("contempt and wrath in plenty", Est 1:18) → decree → anger abates → memory returns.

13110.text: Sequence in Est 5:9–13: glad of heart → seeing Mordecai → wrath → restraint → boasting of riches → "Yet all this is worth nothing to me, so long as I see Mordecai" (5:13).

13111.text: Sequence in Job 32:1–20: the friends fall silent → anger ×3 → waiting from deference and fear → "the spirit in man" → belly like wine with no vent → "I must speak, that I may find relief".

13112.text: Sequence in Psa 37:1–9: seeing the wicked prosper → heating oneself (fret) + envy → "trust … commit … be still … wait" → "refrain from anger" → the wicked fade, the waiting inherit.

13113.text: Sequence in Psa 55:3–5: the enemy's noise → their anger bears a grudge → "my heart is in anguish within me" → terrors of death → fear and trembling.

13114.text: Sequence in Isa 7:2–9: news of alliance → hearts shake like trees → "do not fear … do not let your heart be faint … at the fierce anger" → the anger shrunk to smoking stubs → "if you are not firm in faith …".

13115.text: Sequence in Jer 15:16–20: words eaten → delight of my heart → sitting alone → filled with indignation → unceasing pain → call to return → "a fortified wall … I am with you".

13117.text: Sequence in Jer 37:13–17: false charge ("deserting") → denial ("It is a lie") → officials enraged → beating, prison → the king asks secretly for the word.

13118.text: Sequence in Dan 3:12–28: refusal reported → furious rage → questioned → "but if not … we will not serve" → face changed, furnace heated → deliverance → the king blesses the refusal.

13119.text: Sequence in Jon 3:10–4:11: God relents → Jonah angry → prayer quoting "slow to anger" → asks to die → "Do you do well to be angry?" → shade, plant, worm, wind → asks to die again → "angry enough to die" → God's comparison: pity for a plant, pity for Nineveh → (no answer).

13120.text: Sequence in Mar 3:4–6: a plain question → silence → Jesus looks with anger, grieved at hardness of heart → healing → the plot to destroy him.

13121.text: Sequence in Luk 4:26–30: grace to outsiders told → hearing → filled with wrath → driven to the cliff → he passes through their midst.

13122.text: Sequence in Luk 15:25–32: music heard → the servant explains → angry, refuses to go in → the father comes out and entreats → the ledger ("these many years") → "this son of yours" → "this your brother" → (no answer).

13123.text: Sequence in Act 7:53–58: accusation heard → sawn through in their hearts → teeth ground → Stephen full of the Spirit sees glory → they stop their ears → rush, cast out, stone.

13125.text: Sequence in Exo 32:10–14; Deu 9:7–22: provocation → anger → "let me alone" → intercession from fear, with fasting → relented → the memory made into a warning against self-righteousness.

13126.text: Sequence in Num 11:1–15, 33: complaint → fire → cry to Moses → prayer → craving → Moses asks to die → plague.

13127.text: Sequence in Deu 1:32–38; 3:23–28; 4:21–24: unbelief → anger at the people and at Moses "because of you" → plea refused → sight given → successor charged → warning to others.

13128.text: Sequence in Deu 29:18–29: heart turning / blessing itself → anger smokes, no forgiveness → ruin → onlookers ask why → answer → secret and revealed things.

13129.text: Sequence in Jos 7; 22:10–34: one man takes → anger on all → defeat → offender removed → anger turns → the memory drives a later confrontation → answer "He knows".

13130.text: Sequence in Judg 2:10–23; 10:6–16: a generation not knowing → provocation → given over → distress → cry / confession → pity → deliverer → relapse, worse.

13131.text: Sequence in 2Sa 24:1–17 (+ 1Ch 27:24): anger → incitement → objection overruled → act → heart strikes → "fall into the hand of the Lord" → "let your hand be against me".

13133.text: Sequence in 2Ch 28:9–15: human rage "up to heaven" → prophet names God's wrath → chiefs fear added guilt → captives clothed, fed, carried home.

13134.text: Sequence in 2Ch 32:24–26: healed → no return for the benefit → proud heart → wrath → humbled for the pride of his heart → deferred.

13137.text: Sequence in Psa 106:19–45: forgot God → Moses in the breach → despised the land → Peor → Phinehas, "counted to him as righteousness" → Meribah, Moses' loss → child sacrifice → given to nations → "he heard their cry … relented".

13139.text: Sequence in Isa 9:8–10:7: pride in rebuilding → struck → "did not turn" → leaders mislead → self-devouring → "his hand is stretched out still" (×5) → Assyria as rod, with a heart of its own.

13140.text: Sequence in Isa 51:17–23: cup drunk to the dregs → "There is none to guide her" → sons fainted, "full of the wrath" → cup taken, given to the tormentors.

13141.text: Sequence in Isa 57:14–18: God dwells with the contrite spirit → "nor will I always be angry; for the spirit would grow faint before me" → struck, hid face → backsliding "in the way of his own heart" → "I will heal him".

13142.text: Sequence in Isa 63:1–64:12: no one to help → God's arm alone → "I will recount the steadfast love" → "you were angry, and we sinned" → no one who calls → "we are the clay … please look".

13143.text: Sequence in Jer 7:16–29: intercession forbidden → whole families provoke → "Is it I whom they provoke? … themselves" → wrath poured → "did not accept discipline" → "cut off your hair … lament".

13144.text: Sequence in Jer 18:18–23: plots against the prophet → "remember how I stood before you … to turn away your wrath" → pit dug for his life → "deal with them in the time of your anger".

13147.text: Sequence in Eze 9:1–10: abominations → mark on those who sigh and groan → slaughter begins at the sanctuary → the prophet alone, face down: "Will you destroy all the remnant?" → "my eye will not spare".

13150.text: Sequence in Eze 22:17–31: dross → melted in the furnace → every rank has failed → "I sought for a man … and stand in the breach … but I found none" → indignation poured out.

13151.text: Sequence in Joe 2:11–14; Jon 3:5–10: the day, "who can endure it?" → return with the heart, fasting, sackcloth → the creed (Joel) or the preached word (Nineveh) → "Who knows?" → (Jonah) God relented.

13152.text: Sequence in Mic 7:7–20: "I will look to the Lord" → the enemy gloats → "I will bear the indignation … because I have sinned" → vindication → "Who is a God like you …? He does not retain his anger forever".

13153.text: Sequence in Rom 1:16–2:10: gospel, righteousness by faith → wrath revealed against suppression of the truth → without excuse → judging others → presuming on kindness → hard heart storing up wrath → to each by works.

13154.text: Sequence in Rom 12:17–21: repay no evil → live peaceably → never avenge yourselves: leave it to the wrath of God → feed the enemy → overcome evil with good.

13156.text: The answer the texts give to human anger is most often a question or a reframing, not a rebuke: God's question to Cain (Gen 4:6) and to Jonah (Jon 4:4, 9); Joseph's "not you ... but God" (Gen 45:8); the father's "this your brother" (Luk 15:32); Nathan's parable turned round (2Sa 12:7); in two of these, Jonah and the elder brother, the text ends before the angry one answers.

13157.text: The anger is repeatedly said to end, or to have a purpose past itself: knowledge (Eze 5:13), calm (Eze 16:42), an appointed end (Dan 8:19), "finished" (Rev 15:1), deliverance (1Th 1:10).

13158.text: One characteristic leads to another where the verse says so, set against with "but": "A soft answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger" (Pro 15:1).

13159.text: Anger is named together with another characteristic in one breath or list: "the anger and envy that you showed" (Eze 35:11); "with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart" (Mar 3:5).

13160.text: Anger and Inner seat (M47): Anger answers a heart turned; burns within; the heat of the spirit; a hard heart stores up wrath; anger lodges in the heart of fools.

13161.text: Anger and Wickedness (M58); sin (M56): The cause named before the anger: "because of the evil of your deeds"; "Fret not yourself; it tends only to evil"; "one given to anger causes much transgression".

13162.text: Anger and Desire, jealousy, envy (M18): Jealousy named with God's anger; "jealousy makes a man furious"; "the anger and envy that you showed because of your hatred"; "You covet and cannot obtain, so you fight and quarrel".

13163.text: Anger and Knowing (M15); being heard (M41): Kindled on hearing; its stated end is knowing ("they shall know that I am the Lord"); understanding "in the latter days"; the book heard and the wrath recognised; ears stopped.

13164.text: Anger and Speech and tongue (M65): A harsh word stirs it; speech about God answered with anger; rash words from an embittered spirit; "slow to speak, slow to anger"; slander and obscene talk in the lists.

13165.text: Anger and Faintness (M24); discouragement (M20): "Your sons have fainted … full of the wrath of the Lord"; "for the spirit would grow faint before me"; "lest they become discouraged".

13166.text: Anger and Violence (M10): "For in their anger they killed men"; "killed them in a rage that has reached up to heaven"; Herod's killing at Bethlehem.

13168.text: Anger and Malice and enmity (M06): Hatred named as the source of anger and envy; Job reads the anger as being hated; malice beside anger in the lists.

13169.text: Anger and Fear (M01): Moses afraid of the anger, and heard; afraid, then enraged; angry, then afraid; "do not fear" at another's fierce anger; "not being afraid of the anger of the king"; indignation and fear in one verse.

13170.text: Anger and Wisdom and folly (M16): "Whoever is slow to anger has great understanding"; "A man of quick temper acts foolishly"; folly ruins a man's way and "his heart rages against the Lord"; "a heart of wisdom" asked under the anger.

13171.text: Anger and Prayer (M42): "how long will you be angry with your people's prayers?"; Samuel "cried to the Lord all night"; "lifting holy hands without anger".

13172.text: Anger and Grief and lament (M03): "grieved for David"; "with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart"; a lament raised for "the generation of his wrath"; the provocation asked about inside a lament; godly grief produced indignation; kaʿas rendered "grief".

13173.text: Anger and Grace and mercy (M50); kindness (M05): "being compassionate … he restrained his anger often"; "merciful and gracious, slow to anger"; "for I am merciful"; "But God, being rich in mercy"; "should not you have had mercy"; "Be kind to one another".

13174.text: Anger and Pride (M08): "his heart was proud. Therefore wrath came upon him"; "look on everyone who is proud and abase him"; ʿebrāh rendered "arrogant pride".

13175.text: Anger and Rest and peace (M33): "Therefore I swore in my wrath, 'They shall not enter my rest'"; Tyre and Sidon "asked for peace"; "let them make peace with me".

13176.text: Anger and Turning and repentance (M11): "Who knows? God may turn and relent"; "when he humbled himself the wrath of the Lord turned from him"; "Bear fruit in keeping with repentance"; godly grief "produces a repentance".

13177.text: Anger and Shame (M07): "They shall be ashamed of their harvests because of the fierce anger"; the provocation is "to their own shame"; the incensed "put to shame"; Ezra "ashamed to ask the king".

13178.text: Anger and Memory (M81): "Remember and do not forget how you provoked the Lord your God to wrath"; "Because you have not remembered the days of your youth, but have enraged me"; when the anger abated "he remembered Vashti"; "God remembered Babylon".

13179.text: Anger and Patience (M34): "With patience a ruler may be persuaded" (the same ʾaph); God "has endured with much patience vessels of wrath"; "Be still before the Lord and wait patiently for him" beside "Refrain from anger".

13180.text: Anger and Authority (M72): Mostly tagging (king, hand, master). In the verses: the ruler's anger becomes a command; "A king's wrath is like the growling of a lion"; the authority carries out God's wrath.

13181.text: Anger and Life and death (M25): "the wrath of God remains on him"; "A king's wrath is a messenger of death"; "angry enough to die"; held (OT-08).

13182.text: Anger and Inner seat (M47), side by side with fear: fear side, fear felt in the heart; given in the heart; the heart firm and not afraid (1Sa 28:5; Jer 32:40; Psa 112:7); anger side, anger answers a heart turned; burns within; the heat of the spirit; a hard heart stores up wrath (1Ki 11:9; Est 1:12; Eze 3:14; Rom 2:5).

13183.text: Anger and Faintness (M24), side by side with fear: fear side, "Do not fear or be dismayed" (Deu 31:8); anger side, "for the spirit would grow faint before me" (Isa 57:16).

13184.text: Anger and Knowing (M15); hearing (M41), side by side with fear: fear side, the fear of the Lord as the beginning of knowledge; fear comes by hearing (Pro 1:7; Act 5:5); anger side, kindled on hearing; its stated end is knowing (Num 11:1; Eze 5:13).

13185.text: Anger and Speech (M65), side by side with fear: fear side, fear silences; bends speech into a lie (1Sa 3:15; Gen 18:15); anger side, a harsh word stirs it; rash words from an embittered spirit (Pro 15:1; Psa 106:33).

13186.text: Anger and Wisdom and folly (M16), side by side with fear: fear side, "the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom" (Job 28:28); anger side, "Whoever is slow to anger has great understanding" (Pro 14:29).

13187.text: Anger and Wickedness (M58), side by side with fear: fear side, fear of God joined with turning from evil (Pro 16:6); anger side, the cause named before the anger (Jer 4:4).

13188.text: Anger and Pride (M08), side by side with fear: fear side, "do not become proud, but fear" (Rom 11:20); anger side, "his heart was proud. Therefore wrath came upon him" (2Ch 32:25).

13189.text: Anger and Rest and peace (M33), side by side with fear: fear side, "none shall make you afraid" (Lev 26:6); anger side, "They shall not enter my rest" (Psa 95:11).

13190.text: Anger and Shame (M07), side by side with fear: fear side, horror listed with reproach (Jer 24:9); anger side, "They shall be ashamed of their harvests because of the fierce anger" (Jer 12:13).

13191.text: Anger and Grief (M03), side by side with fear: fear side, rāgaz rendered "deeply moved" (2Sa 18:33); anger side, "with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart" (Mar 3:5).

13192.text: Anger and Turning (M11), side by side with fear: fear side, fear among the fruits of godly grief (2Cor 7:10–11); anger side, godly grief "produces a repentance", and indignation (2Cor 7:10–11).

13193.text: Anger and Life and death (M25), side by side with fear: fear side, "a fountain of life"; "fear of death" (Pro 14:27; Heb 2:15); held; anger side, "the wrath of God remains on him" (Joh 3:36); held (OT-08).

13194.text: Anger and Each other, side by side with fear: fear side, rāgaz (to tremble) rendered "Be angry" (Psa 4:4); fear and wrath in one verse (Psa 90:11); anger side, Moses afraid of the anger (Deu 9:19); afraid, then enraged (Dan 11:30); not afraid of the king's anger (Heb 11:27).

13195.text: The two strands share a verse in Deu 9:19, Psa 90:11, Dan 11:30 and Heb 11:27, and in 2Cor 7:11, where indignation and fear stand in one list.

13196.text: What sets God's anger off: broke the covenant → anger → given over (Judg 2:14, 20); heard → anger → fire (Num 11:1); hearts diamond-hard, lest they hear → therefore great anger (Zec 7:12); blood left uncovered → wrath roused (Eze 24:8); mocking the messengers → wrath rose → no remedy (2Ch 36:16); proud heart → wrath came (2Ch 32:25); suppress the truth → wrath revealed (Rom 1:18).

13197.text: What sets a person's anger off: demand → anger → "Am I in the place of God" (Gen 30:1–2); no regard → very angry → face fell (Gen 4:5); saw no homage → filled with fury → sought to destroy all the Jews (Est 3:5–6); "I thought" → rage (2Ki 5:11–12); afraid → withdraw → enraged (Dan 11:30); heard → filled with wrath → drove him out (Luk 4:28–29); passions at war within → quarrels (Jam 4:1).

13198.text: What turns or ends God's anger: humbled → wrath turned (2Ch 12:12); Moses prayed → the Lord listened (Deu 9:19); stood in the breach → wrath turned (Psa 106:23); atonement → stood between → plague stopped (Num 16:46–48); jealous with my jealousy → wrath turned back (Num 25:11); wrath satisfied → calm, no more angry (Eze 16:42); with the last plagues → the wrath is finished (Rev 15:1).

13199.text: What restrains it, by the verse's reason: compassionate → did not stir up all his wrath (Psa 78:38); "I said I would pour out my wrath" → acted for my name (Eze 20:8–9); heart recoils → will not execute burning anger, for I am God and not a man (Hos 11:8–9); not always angry, for the spirit would grow faint (Isa 57:16); feared the enemy's provocation → not wiped out (Deu 32:26–27).

13200.text: What does not turn it: godless, folly spoken → anger not turned (Isa 9:17); Manasseh's provocations → did not turn from the burning (2Ki 23:26); sought a man to stand in the breach → found none → poured out my indignation (Eze 22:30–31).

13201.text: What follows its end: anger turned → comfort (Isa 12:1); drove them in wrath → gather, bring back, dwell in safety (Jer 32:37); anger abated → he remembered (Est 2:1); "how long … angry these seventy years?" → gracious and comforting words (Zec 1:12–13).

13202.text: What a person's anger leads to: heard → anger → broke the tablets (Exo 32:19); angry → put them in custody (Gen 40:2–3); company of the angry → learning his ways → a snare (Pro 22:24–25); fret → tends only to evil (Psa 37:8); angry → afraid (2Sa 6:8–9); angry → cried to the Lord all night (1Sa 15:11); Naboth's word → vexed and sullen → would eat no food (1Ki 21:4); provoke your children → lest they become discouraged (Col 3:21).

13203.text: What turns or settles a person's anger: soft answer → wrath turned (Pro 15:1); good sense → slow to anger (Pro 19:11); Aaron's answer → Moses heard → approved (Lev 10:16–20); servants' question → dipped → flesh restored (2Ki 5:13–14); poured out her soul, "Go in peace" → ate, face no longer sad (1Sa 1:15–18); sold me → angry with yourselves → do not, for God sent me (Gen 45:5); remember your brother has something against you → first be reconciled (Mat 5:23–24).

13204.text: What the one who carries it out adds: gave them into your hand → you showed no mercy (Isa 47:6); angry but a little → they furthered the disaster → exceedingly angry with them (Zec 1:15); killed in a rage → "Have you not sins of your own?" (2Ch 28:9–10); did not carry out → "the Lord has done this thing to you" (1Sa 28:18).

13205.text: Anger answered in kind: no god, idols → provoked → "I will … provoke them" (Deu 32:21); pours wrath on neighbours → the Lord's cup comes around to you (Hab 2:15–16); they would not hear → I would not hear (Zec 7:13).

13206.text: God's heart is named with his anger three times: "My heart recoils within me" before "I will not execute my burning anger" (Hos 11:8–9); "the intents of his heart" (Jer 23:20); "the day of vengeance was in my heart, and my year of redemption had come" (Isa 63:4).

13207.text: "Slow to anger" is one phrase (Exo 34:6; Pro 14:29): God's proclaimed name, used by many speakers to different ends, and the wise man's virtue.

13208.text: A spirit as the angry party: the devil's great wrath "because he knows that his time is short" (Rev 12:12).

13209.text: How God meets a person's anger: by asking. "Why are you angry?" (Gen 4:6); "Do you do well to be angry?" (Jon 4:4); and the face that falls is Cain's anger and God's withheld anger, "for I am merciful" (Jer 3:12).

13210.text: The provocation is spoken of as between persons: to his face, behind his back, after being "exalted … out of the dust" (1Ki 16:2), and asked about in grief (Jer 8:19).

13211.text: The fierce anger is the anger that turns (ḥārôn with "turn" in 12 of 40 verses); Josiah's whole-hearted turning beside the burning not turned (2Ki 23:25–26); turning asked for without a guarantee ("It may be", Jer 36:7; "perhaps", Zep 2:3; "Who knows?", Jon 3:9); inner acts named as turning it (humbling, a resolve in the heart).

13212.text: Time on each side: God's anger has a stated end ("for a moment", Isa 54:8; "the appointed time of the end", Dan 8:19; "finished", Rev 15:1), and the people are told how to wait (Isa 26:20); a man's anger "kept … forever" (Amo 1:11) is cursed (Gen 49:7).

13213.text: Restraint has stated reasons, all in God: compassion, his name before the nations, the spirit that would faint, "for I am merciful" (Jer 3:12), their humbling; and "I have no wrath" of the vineyard he keeps.

13214.text: The ruler's anger and those beneath it: a command follows at once; the wise appease it; it is "like the growling of a lion" (Pro 19:12).

13215.text: Anger aimed at God: at what he does (Moses, David, Samuel, Jonah), in hunger, and in folly's ruin, where "his heart rages against the Lord" (Pro 19:3).

13216.text: The anger's stated outcome is knowing or understanding ("they shall know that I am the Lord", Eze 5:13; "In the latter days you will understand it clearly", Jer 23:20).

13218.text: Cross-cluster associations, no re-tagging (#1970): qînāh (lament) with grief (M03); indignation with grief and fear (2Cor 7:11); provoking with discouragement (Col 3:21); jealousy and envy in the lists (M18); zeal with zestos; anger at another's honour with no verse naming envy (Gen 4:5; 1Sa 18:8).

13223.text: It belongs with the cup (Isa 51; Jer 25), which is in no chapter (10.0 (what comes back): Holds Hab 2:15 alone).

13224.text: The verses name the acts each time (Ch 13 How it is provoked: Names inner roots from other verses; the outward acts kāʿas names are there only through Jer 7:18).

13225.text: Col 3:6–8 sets God's wrath and the anger to be put away in one paragraph (12 When the inner being goes wrong: Holds God's wrath verses (Col 3:6; Eph 2:3; Rom 2:5) beside the human anger lists).

13242.text: In the narratives the seat is often named by someone else: Eliab names David's heart (1Sa 17:28); Jesus' anger is at his opponents' hardened heart (Mar 3:5).

Ch 13 quotes Jer 23:20 and Hos 11:9, but not Hos 11:8's heart line beside them (Hos 11:8 is in Ch 11 only). Proposed RS for the Ch 13 cross-check (OT-13).; Where: Ch 13; #1890 findings.

13357.text: F.1: What emerged: The word is heat and a poured liquid, and the verses keep both pictures. It is "poured" in 26 of 118 verses, "poured out and kindled" in one clause (Jer 44:6), drunk from a cup, and venom (AG-60, 82, 85).; What it changes elsewhere: 10.13 should describe anger in the word's own pictures (heat, pouring, drinking, poison), not only as a state. Ch 13 has the fire, and lacks the cup.; Where: 10.13; Ch 13.

13358.text: F.2: What emerged: God's heart named a third time with his anger: "the day of vengeance was in my heart, and my year of redemption had come" (Isa 63:4), where his wrath "upheld" him because no one helped (Isa 63:5, AG-70).; What it changes elsewhere: Extends unit 1 F.2 (Hos 11:8; Jer 23:20) and #1890. Proposed RS for the Ch 13 cross-check (OT-13).; Where: Ch 13; #1890 findings.

13360.text: F.5: What emerged: Jealous wrath faces against the people and for them. Jealous fury is set in the setting of adultery for God (Eze 16:38) and for a husband (Pro 6:34) (AG-73, 74).; What it changes elsewhere: Extends AG-04; the overview's part C (what changes its nature) gains a factor: against whom the bond is defended.; Where: overview C.

13361.text: F.6: What emerged: Wrath ends, for God and king, and something follows its end: calm, no more anger (Eze 16:42); after it abated, he remembered (Est 2:1) (AG-76, 77).; What it changes elsewhere: 10.3 holds Est 2:1; Eze 16:43 adds that not remembering enraged him. The two sit in 10.3's territory (remembering) from opposite sides.; Where: 10.3.

13362.text: F.7: What emerged: Fear and wrath meet in this unit: Moses afraid of the wrath (Deu 9:19); alarm, then fury (Dan 11:44); fearing the oppressor's wrath, having forgotten the Maker (Isa 51:13); "who can stand?" (Nah 1:6) (AG-86, 95, 97, 72).; What it changes elsewhere: Input for overview part F (anger with the other characteristics), from the fear side of 10.12.; Where: 10.12; overview F.

13363.text: F.8: What emerged: Restraint has three stated reasons in this unit: his name before the nations (three times in Eze 20), compassion, their humbling; and of the vineyard he keeps he says "I have no wrath" (Isa 27:4, AG-78 to AG-80).; What it changes elsewhere: Extends AN-82; Isa 27:4 is new to the narrative (NS in 10.13).; Where: 10.13; Ch 13.

13364.text: F.9: What emerged: Wrath within the act of gathering and ruling (Eze 20:33–34; Jer 32:37, AG-81).; What it changes elsewhere: Not in the chapters. With AN-95 (the hand's position), a candidate for 11 §4.; Where: 11 §4; 10.13.

13365.text: F.10: What emerged: The heat family runs outside the tag, into the heart (Psa 39:3), lust (Isa 57:5) and blood-vengeance (Deu 19:6).; What it changes elsewhere: Open thread OT-15 (§E; added, #1967).; Where: register.

13449.text: F.3: What emerged: The fierce anger is the anger that turns. "Turn" stands with ḥārôn in 12 of 40 verses. Both use the words do well; one ends in murder, the other in God's unanswered question about pity (AG-138).; What it changes elsewhere: Each is in the chapters on its own. The pairing is NS for 10.13: how God meets a person's anger.; Where: 10.13.

13637.text: Duration (AN §L.3, extended): do not let the sun go down on your anger; the devil's time is short; the wrath finished with the last plagues; the wrath remains: Verses: Eph 4:26; Rev 12:12; Rev 15:1; Joh 3:36.

13638.text: Joined with: grief (Mar 3:5); jealousy or envy in 4 of the 6 lists; fear and longing (2Cor 7:11); words of the mouth in 3 of the 6 lists: Verses: Mar 3:5; §AG-222; 2Cor 7:11.

13639.text: Its picture (new): drink and harvest (the cup, the winepress); bowls poured out; the wrath revealed, stored up, remains, coming: Verses: Rev 14:10, 19; Rev 16:1; Rom 1:18; Rom 2:5; Joh 3:36; Col 3:6.

13640.text: Absence as its measure (new): prayer, the overseer and love are each described by anger's absence: Verses: 1Ti 2:8; Tit 1:7; 1Cor 13:5.

13641.text: F.1: What emerged: The Greek splits by word as the Hebrew did. orgē is God's wrath in 29 of 35; orgizō is never God's own anger; thymos is shared (§A.7). The same noun orgē names God's wrath and the anger a person must put away, in one paragraph (Col 3:6, 8, AG-202).; What it changes elsewhere: With unit 4 F.1, 10.13 can state which words are God's and which are shared, for the whole vocabulary. Overview part A.; Where: 10.13; 11 §4.

13642.text: F.6: What emerged: What meets anger decides its end, in the Gospels: the father who comes out (Luk 15:28); the teaching on serving (Mat 20:25–26); a question from their own practice (Luk 13:15); Gamaliel's counsel (Act 5:34).; What it changes elsewhere: Extends unit 4 F.6. Overview part D.; Where: overview D.

13643.text: F.9: What emerged: The cup: God's wrath as a drink (Rev 14:10; 16:19), and Babylon's wine of passion beside it (Rev 14:8) (AG-215, AG-216).; What it changes elsewhere: Extends unit 2's drink (AN §L.2, ḥēmāh). Overview part C (its forms).; Where: overview C.

13644.text: F.10: What emerged: Cross-cluster associations (#1970, no re-tagging): grief (M03) and fear (M01) with indignation (2Cor 7:11); discouragement with provoking (Col 3:21); jealousy and envy in the lists (zēlos, not an M02 word; AN §L.2 watch); zeal with zestos (Rev 3:19).; What it changes elsewhere: For cross-cluster analysis; no tag change.; Where: cross-cluster.

13645.text: suppress the truth → wrath revealed against them (Rom 1:18).

13646.text: hard and impenitent heart → storing up wrath (Rom 2:5); self-seeking, not obey the truth → wrath and fury (2:8).

13647.text: does not obey the Son → shall not see life → the wrath of God remains on him (Joh 3:36).

13648.text: because of these things → the wrath of God comes (Eph 5:6; Col 3:6).

13649.text: law → wrath; no law → no transgression (Rom 4:15).

13650.text: killed, drove out, hindered → fill up the measure of their sins → wrath has come (1Th 2:15–16).

13651.text: go astray in their heart → provoked → swore in my wrath → shall not enter (Heb 3:10–11); exhort one another every day → none hardened (3:13); unable to enter because of unbelief (3:19).

13652.text: who warned you to flee → bear fruit in keeping with repentance (Mat 3:7–8).

13653.text: justified by his blood → saved from the wrath (Rom 5:9); turned from idols → wait for his Son → delivers us from the wrath (1Th 1:9–10).

13654.text: lived in the passions of our flesh → children of wrath; but God, rich in mercy → made us alive (Eph 2:3–5).

13655.text: never avenge → leave it to the wrath of God (Rom 12:19).

13656.text: do wrong → be afraid → he bears the sword (Rom 13:4); be in subjection → to avoid wrath, and for conscience (13:5).

13657.text: the great day of their wrath has come → who can stand? (Rev 6:17).

13658.text: nations raged → but your wrath came → the dead judged, servants rewarded (Rev 11:18).

13659.text: worships the beast → will drink the wine of God's wrath (Rev 14:9–10); with the last plagues → the wrath is finished (15:1); God remembered Babylon → drain the cup (16:19).

13660.text: asked, they were silent → looked with anger, grieved → "Stretch out your hand" → restored (Mar 3:4–5); went out → counsel to destroy him (3:6).

13662.text: should have had mercy → in anger delivered to the jailers → so also my heavenly Father (Mat 18:33–35); killed his servants → the king angry → destroyed, burned (Mat 22:6–7); made excuses → angry → bring in the poor (Luk 14:18–21).

13663.text: thrown down → great wrath, because his time is short (Rev 12:12); furious with the woman → war on her offspring (12:17).

13664.text: anger of man → does not produce the righteousness of God → therefore put away, receive the word (Jam 1:20–21).

13665.text: angry with his brother → liable to judgment (Mat 5:22); remember → leave your gift → first be reconciled (5:23–24).

13666.text: heard → filled with wrath → drove him out (Luk 4:28–29); heard → enraged → wanted to kill → Gamaliel's counsel (Act 5:33–35); heard → enraged → stopped their ears, rushed → stoned (Act 7:54–58); heard → enraged → crying out → confusion (Act 19:28–29).

13667.text: tricked → furious → killed the children (Mat 2:16); Herod angry → they persuaded Blastus → asked for peace, for food (Act 12:20).

13668.text: as seeing him who is invisible → not afraid of the anger of the king (Heb 11:27).

13672.text: heard → angry → refused to go in → father came out and entreated (Luk 15:27–28).

13674.text: godly grief → repentance → salvation; worldly grief → death (2Cor 7:10); godly grief → indignation, fear, longing, zeal (7:11).

13679.text: In the parable the master of the house, told of the excuses, becomes angry and sends his servant to bring in the poor and crippled and blind and lame (Luk 14:21).

13684.text: In Luk 14:21 anger at a refusal turns into a wider invitation: the anger has a stated ground, the excuses reported (14:18-21), and a stated outcome, the poor brought in and the invited shut out (14:24); the poor are the ones the angry master turns to.

13686.text: Saul's anger is kindled "when he heard these words", the threat to Jabesh, with the Spirit of God rushing upon him (1Sa 11:6), and it ends in mercy that gives the day to God: "Not a man shall be put to death this day, for today the Lord has worked salvation in Israel" (1Sa 11:13).

13687.text: Samson: the Spirit's rushing goes with the striking at Ashkelon, and the "hot anger" comes at the end, with its ground given: his wife wept "You only hate me; you do not love me" (Judg 14:16), he told her "because she pressed him hard" (14:17), and his own word is "If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have found out my riddle" (14:18); then "Samson's wife was given to his companion" (14:20).

13688.text: The passage puts Samson's anger (Judg 14:19) with being betrayed through his wife, not with the Spirit; so it differs from Saul's, where the Spirit and the anger come together (1Sa 11:6).

13689.text: "They were enraged" (Act 7:54) is diapriō ("to be sawn through", G1282) with kardia ("heart"); "they ground their teeth at him" puts the anger in the body; against them stands Stephen, "full of the Holy Spirit, gazed into heaven" (7:55); the M47 token is the heart word itself.

13690.text: Two grounds for subjection stand side by side: "to avoid God's wrath" and "for the sake of conscience" (Rom 13:5).

13694.text: The king of Moab "saw that the battle was going against him" and tried to break through, "but they could not" (2Ki 3:26); "Then he took his oldest son who was to reign in his place and offered him for a burnt offering on the wall" (3:27), giving up his own heir and succession at the point of defeat.

13695.text: The wrath in 2Ki 3:27 is qeṣep (H7110A). Where "wrath came upon" a people with no bearer named, the passage gives a breach first (Num 1:53; 18:5; Jos 9:20; 22:20; 1Ch 27:24; 2Ch 24:18; 32:25); in 2Ch 32:25-26 the same wrath is then called "the wrath of the Lord"; in 2Ki 3 no breach is named, and Elisha had said "He will also give the Moabites into your hand" (3:18).

13696.text: The outcome in 2Ki 3: "And they withdrew from him and returned to their own land"; the campaign ends short of the word.

13697.text: The verse leaves open whose wrath it is: the construction elsewhere is God's after a breach; the setting would also allow Moab's fury, roused by the sacrifice, or Israel's own horror at it; the verse does not decide.

13698.text: The teeth are where anger and hostility show, as the hands are for fear: "The wicked man sees it and is angry; he gnashes his teeth and melts away" (Psa 112:10); "The wicked plots against the righteous and gnashes his teeth at him" (Psa 37:12); and Act 7:54.

13700.text: God's anger as the sufferer feels it: "He has torn me in his wrath and hated me; he has gnashed his teeth at me" (Job 16:9).

13703.text: Links that do not count are non-inner-being senses of the M47 word: Pro 25:23, Eze 13:13, 19:12 and Psa 11:6 (wind); Num 11:33 (meat); Eze 16:26 (lustful "flesh"); Eze 7:19 (nephesh as hunger); Psa 124:5 ("us"); Est 8:11 (lives as targets); no M02 Strong's loses its implicit status through this.

13705.text: In the vice lists with thumos (2Cor 12:20; Gal 5:20; Eph 4:31; Col 3:8) the inner place is given by the list's frame, not by a seat: in Gal 5:19 anger is among "the works of the flesh", with 5:17 (flesh against Spirit) nearby; in Col 3:8 it is put away along with speech "from your mouth"; flesh and mouth take the seat's place.

13706.text: In crowd rage (Luk 4:28, "all in the synagogue were filled with wrath"; Act 19:28, "enraged and ... crying out, 'Great is Artemis'") the collective is the container: "filled", with no organ named; the shout carries it.

13707.text: Divine wrath in Revelation (14:10, 19; 15:1, 7; 16:1, 19; 19:15) becomes a substance: wine, a cup, bowls, a winepress; the human side is drinking it (14:10; 16:19); in Rev 14:8 and 18:3 "the wine of the passion of her sexual immorality" the same word means intoxicating passion, and the drinking image is shared with God's wrath.

13708.text: Heb 11:27 is a no-seat verse about Moses's inner operation (faith, not being afraid); the king's anger is only its occasion: "for he endured as seeing him who is invisible".

13712.text: 2Cor 7:11 lists "what indignation, what fear, what longing, what zeal" as the fruit of "godly grief", a sequence of inner operations valued as good; Mar 10:14 is Jesus's indignation, and the bearer class is recorded as divine in the party data, noted and not resolved.

13713.text: Anger turns straight into action, especially in the parables and in narrative: "in anger his master delivered him to the jailers" (Mat 18:34); "The king was angry, and he sent his troops" (Mat 22:7); the master "became angry and said ... bring in the poor" (Luk 14:21); Herod "became furious, and he sent and killed all the male children" (Mat 2:16); there is no interval in which a seat would be named, and the act is the evidence of the state.

13715.text: In Mat 5:21-22 anger is set beside murder, and incurs the same "liable to judgment".

13716.text: Anger is bounded by time in Eph 4:26-27, "Be angry and do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger, and give no opportunity to the devil"; the neighbouring 4:23 has "renewed in the spirit of your minds", and the implicit seat is the passage's.

13717.text: Cholaō (Joh 7:23) is built on cholē, "bile": the Greek carries an inner organ inside the verb, as thumos does.

13718.text: Relational causation: in Eph 6:4 fathers "provoke to anger" (parorgizō), exactly parallel to Col 3:21 (provoke, discouraged); in Rom 10:19 God provokes Israel to jealousy and anger, an inner operation induced from outside, with God as the cause.

13719.text: Gen 4:5-6: "Cain was very angry, and his face fell ... Why are you angry, and why has your face fallen?"; God reads the anger off the face; what follows in 4:7 is an inner struggle stated as an image: "sin is crouching at the door. Its desire is for you, and you must rule over it".

13720.text: Dan 3:19: "Nebuchadnezzar was filled with fury, and the expression of his face was changed"; the rage is externalised onto the furnace, "heated seven times more".

13721.text: 1Ki 21:4: Ahab went home "vexed and sullen ... lay down on his bed and turned away his face and would eat no food"; in 21:5 Jezebel says, "Why is your spirit so vexed that you eat no food?"; the narrator gives no seat, and the wife names one, reading it off the body (1Ki 20:43, "vexed and sullen", is the same pair).

13722.text: 1Sa 20:34: Jonathan "rose from the table in fierce anger and ate no food ... for he was grieved for David"; anger, grief and fasting come together.

13723.text: 2Ki 5:11-14: Naaman "was angry and went away ... turned and went away in a rage"; his inner thought is quoted ("Behold, I thought that he would surely come out"); the servants talk him round (5:13), and "his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child" (5:14): rage, persuasion, obedience, restoration, with no seat word anywhere.

13724.text: 2Ch 16:10 (Asa "in a rage with" the seer) and Dan 2:12 (the king "angry and very furious"): anger issues in orders, imprisonment and execution.

13725.text: Jer 3:12, "I will not look on you in anger", is literally "cause my face to fall": the same body idiom is used of God.

13729.text: Ashan, "smoke", is literally smoke when it is the anger word: Sinai "wrapped in smoke" (Exo 19:18), mountains that "smoke" at his touch (Psa 104:32; 144:5); where it is anger it is divine anger answering a human heart: "the anger of the Lord and his jealousy will smoke against that man" (Deu 29:20), the man of 29:18-19 "whose heart is turning away ... blesses himself in his heart, saying, 'I shall be safe, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart'"; the seat in the passage is the human's secret self-blessing, and the anger answers it.

13730.text: Meribah is a place name that stores an inner event ("the waters of Meribah, where the people of Israel quarreled with the Lord", Num 20:13); in Eze 47:19 and 48:28 it is a boundary marker with no inner content left; in Psa 106:32 the next verse is seated (106:33, "they made his spirit bitter", Moses's spirit).

13732.text: Job's vexation (ka'as H3708B): "Oh that my vexation were weighed" (6:2) and "my eye has grown dim from vexation" (17:7); the eye carries it, and the whole body, "all my members are like a shadow"; Job 5:2, "vexation kills the fool", shows the inner state as lethal.

13734.text: Whose seat the anger points to, The heart that provokes the anger (human, the cause): genuine links Rom 2:5 "your hard and impenitent heart … storing up wrath"; Heb 3:10 "always go astray in their heart"; 1Ki 11:9 "his heart had turned away"; 2Ch 32:25 "his heart was proud"; Zec 7:12 "hearts diamond-hard"; Jer 4:4 "foreskin of your hearts"; Isa 57:17; Pro 19:3 "his heart rages against the Lord". What it implies for the no-seat verses: The long series "the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel" (Num 25:3; Judg 2:14, 20; 3:8; 10:7; 2Ki 13:3 …) and "provoking the Lord to anger" (ka'as H3707: 1Ki 14–16; 2Ki 17, 21; Jer 7, 25, 32, 44) carry the human inner cause by narrative: idolatry, turning, stubbornness. The seat is implicit in the offender, and the anger is its answer. Jer 7:19, "Is it I whom they provoke? … Is it not themselves, to their own shame?", turns the provocation back onto the provokers' own inner being.

13735.text: Whose seat the anger points to, The life or spirit that receives the anger (human, the effect): genuine links Jer 49:37 / 51:45 life; Isa 57:16 "the spirit would grow faint before me"; Job 6:4 "my spirit drinks their poison"; Psa 38:3 flesh. What it implies for the no-seat verses: The laments and penitential psalms: Psa 6:1; 38:1; 88:7, 16 ("your wrath lies heavy upon me"); 90:7, 9 ("by your wrath we are dismayed … we bring our years to an end like a sigh"); Lam 3:1 ("I am the man who has seen affliction under the rod of his wrath"). The receiver's dismay is the inner operation, and the seat is implied from these links.

13736.text: Whose seat the anger points to, The angry party's own seat: genuine links Human: Job 36:13 "the godless in heart cherish anger"; Job 18:4 "you who tear yourself in your anger"; Pro 14:29 / 16:32 (slow to anger with "rules his spirit"); Ecc 7:9 "anger lodges in the heart of fools"; Act 17:16 Paul's "spirit was provoked within him". Divine: Jer 23:20 / 30:24 "the intents of his heart / mind". What it implies for the no-seat verses: The human anger narratives (§2.1 below) and the wisdom sayings (§2.2).

13737.text: Neh 5:6-7: "I was very angry when I heard their outcry ... I took counsel with myself" (Hebrew: my heart counselled me): the anger is followed by deliberation, and the seat arrives with the deliberation.

13739.text: Est 1:12, "his anger burned within him" (Hebrew bo, "in him"), has a pronoun and no seat word; Est 3:5 has Haman "filled with fury", and Est 5:9 is the same scene seated, "joyful and glad of heart. But when Haman saw Mordecai ... he was filled with wrath": the implicit seat for 3:5 is Haman's own heart, established two chapters later.

13740.text: Jon 4:1-3: "it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was angry. And he prayed ... I knew that you are a gracious God ... slow to anger ... please take my life from me": Jonah quotes God's own "slow to anger" against him, so the anger comes from a creed he knows well; God's reply, "Do you do well to be angry?" (4:4, 9), leads to "angry enough to die".

13741.text: Anger with an act: Moses "saw the calf ... anger burned hot, and he threw the tablets" (Exo 32:19); Balaam struck the donkey (Num 22:27); Balak "struck his hands together" (Num 24:10); Saul's verbal assault on Jonathan (1Sa 20:30); David's verdict on the rich man, "the man who has done this deserves to die" (2Sa 12:5), which the next verse turns: "You are the man."

13742.text: Num 11:10, "the anger of the Lord blazed hotly, and Moses was displeased": Moses then complains to God (11:11), the prophet caught between divine anger and the people's weeping.

13743.text: "Slow to anger" (Pro 14:29; 15:18; 16:32; 19:11) is literally "long of nostrils", the same idiom as God's self-description in Exo 34:6 (Num 14:18; Neh 9:17; Psa 86:15; 103:8; 145:8; Jon 4:2; Nah 1:3): a human virtue and a divine attribute share one body idiom.

13744.text: The wisdom sayings treat anger as governable from outside: "a soft answer turns away wrath" (Pro 15:1); "a gift in secret averts anger" (21:14); "the wise turn away wrath" (29:8); "a wise man will appease" the king's wrath (16:14); Jam 1:19-20, "slow to anger; for the anger of man does not produce the righteousness of God", followed at once by "the implanted word, which is able to save your souls" (1:21, seated).

13745.text: The inner place is given by a reflexive, "in himself" or "to themselves" (Est 1:12; Mar 14:4).

13746.text: The inner place is given by frame words: "flesh" (Gal 5; 1Cor 3), "mind / nous" (1Ti 6) and "mouth" (Col 3:8).

13747.text: Human anger is repeatedly shown with no seat, carried by act, face, speech, or another person's naming; where the seat appears, it often comes in the next verse, as a consequence or an explanation (Neh 5:7; 1Ki 21:5; 1Sa 1:15).

13748.text: In Jon 4 the M02 verses (4:1, 4, 9) are no-seat and the seated verse is 4:3 (life); "angry enough to die" (Jon 4:3, 9) belongs with the death-wish passages.

13749.text: 1Ki 21:4-5 (Jezebel naming Ahab's spirit) and 1Sa 1:15-16 (Hannah explaining herself) are both one person reading or naming another's inner state.

13754.text: A human seat is hardened by the person, or with no agent named (68 verses): Pharaoh by himself (Exo 8:15, 32; 9:34); the stiff neck (Exo 32:9 ... Neh 9:29; Jer 7:26; 17:23; 19:15); sherirut, "the stubbornness of their evil heart" (Jer 3:17; 7:24; 9:14; 11:8; 13:10; 16:12; 18:12; 23:17; Deu 29:19); "diamond-hard" hearts (Zec 7:12); Nebuchadnezzar's "spirit was hardened" (Dan 5:20); the New Testament hardness of heart (Mat 19:8; Mar 3:5; 6:52; 8:17; 10:5; 16:14; Rom 2:5; Eph 4:18); Psa 95:8 and its New Testament reuse (Heb 3:8, 13, 15; 4:7).

13756.text: God's own seat in resolve and purpose, none of it hardened: he "said in his heart, 'I will never again curse the ground'" (Gen 8:21); "what is in my heart" (1Sa 2:35); "a man after his own heart" (1Sa 13:14; Act 13:22); "my eyes and my heart will be there" (1Ki 9:3; 2Ch 7:16); 2Ki 10:30; 1Ch 17:19; Psa 33:11; "the day of vengeance was in my heart" (Isa 63:4); "the intents of his heart" (Jer 23:20; 30:24); "with all my heart and all my soul" (Jer 32:41); Job 7:17; 10:13; 34:14.

13761.text: Hardness, heaviness and strength are said of God's hand, arm, sword and breath, not of his heart: "The hand of the Lord was heavy" (1Sa 5:6, 11); "his hand is hard against us" (1Sa 5:7); "your hand was heavy upon me" (Psa 32:4); the "strong hand" of the Exodus (Exo 6:1; 13:9; Deu 4:34); the "thick" rising smoke of his coming in anger (Isa 30:27); "his hard and great and strong sword" (Isa 27:1).

13765.text: Where a hardening or heaviness word is used of God's own disposition, it is negated: "He does not retain [chazaq] his anger forever, because he delights in steadfast love" (Mic 7:18); "the Lord's hand is not shortened ... or his ear dull [kaved, heavy]" (Isa 59:1); "he does not afflict from his heart" (Lam 3:33); "my soul shall not abhor you" (Lev 26:11).

13769.text: The heavy or hard hand, chains, sword and breath (kaved, qashah, qasheh: 1Sa 5:6, 5:7, 5:11; Psa 32:4; Lam 3:7; Isa 27:1, 27:8; Isa 30:27; Jer 20:7; Mat 25:24; Mal 3:13) is spoken of by humans under it, or by the narrator describing them; in this set God never calls his own hand heavy or hard; it is framed as experience: terror, affliction, wasting, being walled in, fear.

13770.text: The "strong / mighty hand and outstretched arm" (chazaq) is the Exodus formula (Exo 6:1; 13:9; Deu 3:24; 4:34; 5:15; 6:21; 7:8; 7:19; 9:26; 11:2; 26:8; Jos 4:24; 1Ki 8:42; 2Ch 6:32; Neh 1:10; Psa 89:13; 136:12; Isa 40:10; Jer 21:5; 32:21; 50:34; Eze 20:33-34; Dan 9:15; Exo 32:11; Pro 23:11), spoken by God, Moses, the creed and prayers; it is framed as deliverance remembered, taught to children (Deu 6:21), and pleaded in prayer (Deu 9:26; Dan 9:15).

13778.text: The same hand is "hard" or "saving" depending on which side one stands: toward Egypt it is "great deeds of terror" (Deu 4:34; 26:8; Jer 32:21), toward Israel it is "brought us out" (Deu 6:21), and in Jer 21:5 Israel finds itself on Egypt's side of the formula, "I myself will fight against you with outstretched hand and strong arm, in anger and in fury"; the hand does not change, the person's position before it changes.

13779.text: The context names as the source of the heavy hand, Righteousness and justice, with steadfast love and faithfulness: "You have a mighty arm; strong is your hand … Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne; steadfast love and faithfulness go before you" (Psa 89:13–14). "The Lord our God is righteous in all the works that he has done" (Dan 9:14), then "who brought your people out … with a mighty hand" (9:15), then "according to all your righteous acts, let your anger … turn away" (9:16)

13781.text: The context names as the source of the heavy hand, Steadfast love (chesed): "with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, for his steadfast love endures forever" (Psa 136:12). The refrain covers the striking of the firstborn (136:10) and the overthrow of Pharaoh (136:15). "He does not retain his anger forever, because he delights in steadfast love" (Mic 7:18)

13784.text: The context names as the source of the heavy hand, Covenant purpose, through judgment: "with a mighty hand … and with wrath poured out I will be king over you … I will enter into judgment with you … and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant" (Eze 20:33–37)

13787.text: The context names as the source of the heavy hand, Anger (named, and set inside a purpose): Jer 21:5 ("in anger and in fury"); Isa 30:27 ("burning with his anger"). The purpose that follows: "the way of life and the way of death" (Jer 21:8); "when the Lord binds up the brokenness of his people, and heals the wounds inflicted by his blow" (Isa 30:26)

13789.text: The heaviness has its source in God's character: the texts name righteousness and justice (Psa 89:14; Dan 9:14, 16) together with steadfast love, faithfulness, the oath, and the cause of the weak; anger is named too, but never as the last word, standing inside a purpose of covenant, atonement and healing.

13795.text: Eze 23:25 is the one verse in the divine set where the agents' own fury is named.

13796.text: The verse Mar 10:14 gives the inner operation, anger with grief, in human terms, as Mar 3:5 does (Mar 3:5 is seated).

13797.text: Jon 4:2 is Jonah's angry prayer quoting "slow to anger" back at God, one passage with Jon 4:1, 4 and 9, which are human.

13798.text: Luk 15:28, the elder brother, is a human figure of anger, on the human side.

13799.text: Rev 12:12 (the devil "in great wrath") and Rev 12:17 (the dragon "became furious") are anger of neither a human nor God.

13801.text: 2Ch 29:8 (4A God's wrath comes upon, goes out against or uproots his people: the cause named): horror is what onlookers see of the wrath.

13802.text: 2Cor 12:20 (5L Anger in the lists of what is put away): Paul fears the quarrel, jealousy and anger he may find.

13803.text: 2Cor 7:11 (5V Indignation produced by godly grief): indignation and fear as fruits of godly grief.

13805.text: 2Sa 22:8 (3C God's fierce anger on the nations and in the day; the earth shakes): parallel of Psa 18:7,.

13808.text: Deu 9:19 (G Intercession before God's anger): Moses afraid of the anger, and heard.

13809.text: Est 5:9 (2Q Wrath at a slight seen or an expectation thwarted): Mordecai neither rose nor trembled; Haman filled with wrath.

13812.text: Heb 11:27 (5P Not afraid of the king's anger): not afraid of the king's anger.

13813.text: Isa 13:13 (4J The day of wrath, and the sayings on whom it falls): the heavens tremble at the wrath.

13814.text: Isa 13:9 (C God angry with nations, enemies, oppressors): desolation is the outcome; the day of wrath is carried through 13:13.

13815.text: Isa 51:13 (2R The oppressor's wrath, feared): fear of the oppressor's wrath where God is forgotten.

13816.text: Isa 5:25 (3A God's anger kindled against his people: the formula, with cause and act): anger not turned (10.13); the quaking mountains are nature, not an inner act.

13817.text: Isa 7:4 (3S Enemies' anger, as the one attacked bears it): do not fear the fierce anger of Rezin.

13818.text: Jer 25:38 (3C God's fierce anger on the nations and in the day; the earth shakes): the land made waste; outcome only.

13819.text: Jer 42:18 (2A God's wrath with his people, city and land: poured out, kindled, not quenched): horror and curse as the outcome of the wrath.

13823.text: Psa 18:7 (3C God's fierce anger on the nations and in the day; the earth shakes): the mountains tremble because he was angry.

13824.text: Psa 55:3 (U Enemies' anger, as the one attacked bears it): the one attacked: "My heart is in anguish within me".

13826.text: Psa 88:16 (3G God's anger borne in lament, or explained): wrath borne without a turn.

13827.text: Psa 88:7 (2K God's wrath in lament and prayer): wrath as weight.

13828.text: Psa 90:11 (4K God's wrath borne: in body, days, prayer and lament): the power of his anger and the fear of him.

13829.text: Rom 13:4 (5E Left to God's wrath; the authority as its servant): be afraid; the authority carries out wrath.

13832.text: Dan 11:30 (4S Anger against one suspected or set against): afraid, then enraged.

13833.text: Isa 26:20 (4G The indignation has a set end): hiding until the fury passes.

13834.text: Isa 54:8 (4F Turned: for a moment, not forever; the reasons given; healed and gathered): anger for a moment, face hidden.

13835.text: Isa 57:17 (4F Turned: for a moment, not forever; the reasons given; healed and gathered): face hidden in anger, and not noticed.

13836.text: Job 14:13 (H God's anger in lament, prayer and thanks): hide me until your wrath be past.

13837.text: Psa 27:9 (H God's anger in lament, prayer and thanks): hide not your face; turn not away in anger.

13838.text: Rev 6:16 (5F The great day of wrath: the wrath of the Lamb; your wrath came): hide us from the wrath of the Lamb.

13839.text: 1Ch 13:10 (3B God's anger against a named person or group): parallel of 2Sa 6:7,.

13840.text: 2Sa 12:5 (3N Indignation for one wronged): David's anger and his oath of death.

13841.text: 2Sa 6:7 (3B God's anger against a named person or group): anger against Uzzah, and his death.

13842.text: Eze 21:31 (4I God's wrath on the nations and enemies; the earth before it): wrath on Ammon; no life word in the verse.

13843.text: Eze 22:20 (A God angry with his people as a whole): parallel of 22:21,.

13844.text: Eze 22:21 (4A God's wrath comes upon, goes out against or uproots his people: the cause named): the breath that gives life named in his anger.

13845.text: Eze 35:11 (Q Anger against a brother, rival or kin, kept or turned): "as I live"; anger and envy from hatred.

13846.text: Eze 6:12 (2E God's wrath spent, satisfied, then calm): death by pestilence, sword and famine; outcome only.

13847.text: Gen 45:5 (3V Angry with oneself): angry with oneself; God sent me to preserve life.

13848.text: Isa 48:9 (D God's anger restrained, deferred, turned, ended): anger deferred for his name.

13849.text: Isa 57:16 (4F Turned: for a moment, not forever; the reasons given; healed and gathered): the spirit would faint.

13850.text: Jer 10:10 (4I God's wrath on the nations and enemies; the earth before it): the living God (Ch 2); the earth quaking at his wrath is carried through Psa 18:7 and Isa 13:13.

13851.text: Jer 18:23 (I God's anger called down on others): Jeremiah prays the anger onto those who dug a pit for his life.

13852.text: Job 4:9 (J God's anger explained, asked about, presumed on): breath, and the blast of his anger.

13853.text: Job 5:2 (3Z The fool's vexation, and anger lodging in the fool): vexation kills the fool.

13854.text: Joh 3:36 (5A God's wrath revealed, stored up, remaining, coming: the cause named): life, or wrath remaining.

13855.text: Jon 4:9 (3U God asks the angry one about his anger): angry enough to die (Ch 2, 10.1, 10.13); see the stale 10.13 note in section 4.

13856.text: Jos 9:20 (4C Wrath guarded against: an order, an oath, a warning, a decree): let them live, lest wrath be upon us.

13857.text: Lev 10:6 (4C Wrath guarded against: an order, an oath, a warning, a decree): mourning held back, lest you die and wrath come.

13858.text: Pro 16:14 (2P The ruler's wrath, and those beneath it): a king's wrath is a messenger of death.

13859.text: Pro 19:11 (V Anger governed: slow, quick, ruled): good sense makes anger long.

13860.text: Psa 124:3 (U Enemies' anger, as the one attacked bears it): swallowed alive in the enemies' anger.

13861.text: Psa 138:7 (U Enemies' anger, as the one attacked bears it): life preserved against the enemies' wrath.

13862.text: Psa 30:5 (D God's anger restrained, deferred, turned, ended): anger for a moment, favour for a lifetime.

13863.text: Psa 78:38 (D God's anger restrained, deferred, turned, ended): anger restrained; they were but flesh.

13864.text: Psa 78:50 (C God angry with nations, enemies, oppressors): a path for his anger; not spared from death.

13865.text: Psa 7:6 (4W Enemies' fury and rush, as the one attacked bears it): arise in your anger, awake for me.

13866.text: Rev 15:7 (5G The cup, the winepress, the bowls: the wrath finished): the bowls of the wrath of God who lives forever; no inner act.

13867.text: 1Sa 20:30 (3O Anger at a rival honoured, a brother, or a work going forward): Saul's anger at Jonathan's choice.

13868.text: 1Ti 2:8 (5M A person's anger governed: be angry and do not sin; slow to anger; at a brother; in prayer; in the overseer; not in love): prayer without anger or quarrelling.

13869.text: Act 5:33 (5N Enraged at a word heard: crowds and councils, the nations): enraged, and wanted to kill them.

13870.text: Deu 29:20 (A God angry with his people as a whole): not willing to forgive; anger and jealousy smoke.

13871.text: Eze 20:8 (2F God's wrath held back, not stirred, not poured): not willing to listen; wrath said, and held back.

13872.text: Psa 106:23 (2J Intercession before God's wrath): his chosen one stood in the breach.

13874.text: Pro 20:2, "The terror of a king is like the growling of a lion; whoever provokes him to anger forfeits his life", sets the fear of a ruler beside the anger of the ruler and says what provoking him costs; the verse after says what to do instead, "It is an honor for a man to keep aloof from strife, but every fool will be quarreling" (20:3), and the verse before names wine as "a brawler" (20:1).

13875.text: What a person does with the terror of a king is left to him, either keeping aloof or quarrelling (Pro 20:1-3).

13876.text: Job tells his friends "be afraid of the sword, for wrath brings the punishment of the sword, that you may know there is a judgment" (Job 19:29) straight after "I know that my Redeemer lives" and "My heart faints within me!" (19:25, 27), answering "How we will pursue him!" and "The root of the matter is found in him" (19:28); he tells his accusers to fear, and the reason he gives is that there is a judgment.

13877.text: The one being accused turns the fear of wrath back onto those who pursue him, from the confidence he has just stated (Job 19:29).

13878.text: In Lam 2:22 the lament speaks to God about his anger, "Look, O Lord, and see! With whom have you dealt thus?" (2:20), "you have killed them in the day of your anger, slaughtering without pity" (2:21); the figure is a call to a feast, and a festival day gathers people to rejoice, but here what is gathered is "my terrors on every side".

13879.text: The speaker of Lam 2:22 does not turn away from God in the terror: he asks him to look, and names what his anger did to those "I held and raised".

13881.text: Two angers stand in one sentence in Rev 11:18: "The nations raged, but your wrath came"; in the same verse fear of his name is what is rewarded, "both small and great"; the elders say this in worship (11:16-17).

13882.text: Deu 31:17 runs the whole course in God's own words, "my anger will be kindled against them ... I will forsake them and hide my face from them, and they will be devoured"; the cause stands on both sides of the verse: "they will forsake me and break my covenant" (31:16), and "I will surely hide my face in that day because of all the evil that they have done, because they have turned to other gods" (31:18).

13883.text: The people's question in Deu 31:17, "Have not these evils come upon us because our God is not among us?", names the absence but not the turning that the verses give as its cause.

13884.text: Jer 33:5, "whom I shall strike down in my anger and my wrath, for I have hidden my face from this city because of all their evil", is followed by a turn, "Behold, I will bring to it health and healing, and I will heal them" (33:6): in two verses the hidden face and the anger are followed straight away by healing.

13885.text: Psa 89:46, "How long, O Lord? Will you hide yourself forever? How long will your wrath burn like fire?", sets the length of the anger against the length of the psalmist's own life: "Remember how short my time is!" (89:47); then "What man can live and never see death?" (89:48).

13886.text: The plea in Psa 89:46-48 weighs God's anger against a short life.
