17217.text: What changes or stops an operation: a gift (Pro 21:14).

17220.text: What changes or stops an operation: a time limit: do not let the sun go down on your anger (Eph 4:26).

17223.text: Method 3 of carrying an inner operation, an inner place outside M47 (a body word or pronoun), internal: chob, bosom (Job 31:33); chambers of the belly (Pro 18:8); in himself (Act 10:17); within him (Est 1:12).

17227.text: The seat often arrives in the next verse, as explanation or consequence: Neh 5:6 to 7; 1 Kgs 21:4 to 5; 1 Sam 1:7 to 15; Deu 1:27 to 28; Phil 4:6 to 7.

17231.text: cheq (H2436, bosom) is mostly physical (lap, embrace) but has seat-of-emotion usage (Ecc 7:9, anger rests in the bosom of fools; Ps 35:13); flagged, not auto-added, a researcher call.

17236.text: d. Thinking, planning, understanding, remembering: *Plans and devising:* Pro 16:1, 9; 19:21; 6:14, 18; 24:2; 12:20; Psa 140:2; 58:2; Zec 7:10; 8:17; Isa 10:7; Act 5:4; Eze 38:10.; *Understanding and knowing:*; "a heart to understand" (Deu 29:4); "understanding mind" (1Ki 3:9); "understand with their hearts" (Isa 6:10; Mat 13:15; Joh 12:40; Act 28:27); "an intelligent heart acquires knowledge" (Pro 18:15); "the heart of the hasty will understand" (Isa 32:4); *Remembering and "laying to heart":*; Isa 47:7; 57:1, 11; 42:25; Mal 2:2; Jer 12:11; Ecc 7:2; 9:1; Deu 4:39; 32:46; 1Sa 21:12; "call to mind" (Lam 3:21; Deu 30:1); "come into mind" (Jer 3:16; 7:31; 19:5; 32:35; 44:21; 51:50; Isa 65:17); Haggai's repeated "Consider your ways" is literally *set your heart* (Hag 1:5, 7; 2:15, 18) [lexical].; *Searching and investigating:* "I applied my heart to seek and to search out" (Ecc 1:13, 17; 7:25; 8:9, 16); "great searchings of heart" (Judg 5:15–16).; *Pondering and treasuring:* Mary "treasured up all these things, pondering them in her heart" (Luk 2:19, 51); "ponder in your own hearts on your beds" (Psa 4:4); "the meditation of my heart" (Psa 19:14; 49:3).; *Questioning and reasoning:* Mar 2:6, 8; Luk 3:15; 5:22; 9:47; 24:38.

17237.text: e. Willing, deciding, purposing, being moved: *Deciding:*; "Daniel resolved" (Dan 1:8); "Joash decided" (2Ch 24:4); "has determined this in his heart" (1Co 7:37); "Each one must give as he has decided in his heart" (2Co 9:7); "of my own will / accord" (Num 24:13; 16:28, lēv); "It is in my heart to make a covenant" (2Ch 29:10); "I had it in my heart to build a house" (1Ch 22:7; 28:2; 1Ki 8:17–18); *Being moved to give:* "everyone whose heart stirred him … and everyone whose spirit moved him" (Exo 35:21); also Exo 25:2; 35:5, 22, 26, 29; 36:2; 2Ki 12:4 ("the money that a man's heart prompts him to bring").; *Intention as depth:* "The purpose in a man's heart is like deep water, but a man of understanding will draw it out" (Pro 20:5); "the inward mind and heart of a man are deep" (Psa 64:6).

17239.text: g. Moral character and orientation: *Qualities:* pure, upright, blameless, whole, perfect (1Ki 8:61; 15:14; Psa 24:4; 73:1; Mat 5:8; 2Ti 2:22); crooked, perverse, evil, deceitful, proud, haughty, stubborn (Pro 11:20; 17:20; 16:5; Jer 17:9; Jer 7:24 and the "stubbornness of their evil heart" series; Eze 28:2, 17; Obd 3).; *Direction:*; turns (1Ki 11:3–4, 9; Deu 29:18; 30:17), inclines (Psa 119:36, 112; 141:4; Jos 24:23; Judg 9:3), goes after (Eze 11:21; 20:16; 33:31; Job 31:7), is set on (Psa 62:10; Dan 11:28); is near or far (Isa 29:13; Mat 15:8; Mar 7:6); is "toward" someone (1Ch 29:18; 2Ch 16:9); "For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also" (Mat 6:21; Luk 12:34); *Whole vs divided:* "with all their heart / whole heart" (many verses; e.g. Psa 119:2, 10, 34, 58, 69, 145; 138:1; Jer 24:7; 29:13; 2Ch 15:15; 31:21); "not with a whole heart" (2Ch 25:2); "double heart" (Psa 12:2); "unite my heart to fear your name" (Psa 86:11); "one heart" (Jer 32:39; 2Ch 30:12; Eze 11:19); "purify your hearts, you double-minded" (Jam 4:8).

17241.text: i. The heart as a surface, container, store, soil: *Written on:*; "write them on the tablet of your heart" (Pro 3:3; 7:3); sin "engraved on the tablet of their heart" (Jer 17:1); "I will write it on their hearts" (Jer 31:33; Heb 8:10; 10:16); "tablets of human hearts" (2Co 3:3); "written on our hearts" (2Co 3:2); "the work of the law is written on their hearts" (Rom 2:15); *Stored in:*; "I have stored up your word in my heart" (Psa 119:11); "lay up these words … in your heart" (Deu 11:18; Job 22:22); "keep them within your heart" (Pro 4:21); "laid them up in their hearts" (Luk 1:66); "the good treasure of his heart" (Luk 6:45); *Things put in or taken in:*; "idols into their hearts" (Eze 14:3–7); "eternity into man's heart" (Ecc 3:11); "the law of his God is in his heart" (Psa 37:31; Isa 51:7); "the fear of me in their hearts" (Jer 32:40); "wisdom rests in the heart" (Pro 14:33); "wisdom will come into your heart" (Pro 2:10); *Soil:* "hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bear fruit" (Luk 8:15); "what has been sown in his heart" snatched away (Mat 13:19; Luk 8:12).; *Vessel filled:* "Satan filled your heart" (Act 5:3); "sorrow has filled your heart" (Joh 16:6); "hearts full of evil" (Ecc 9:3); "hearts overflow with follies" (Psa 73:7).

17242.text: j. The heart's own "senses": fringe: "having the eyes of your hearts enlightened" (Eph 1:18); "God … has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge" (2Co 4:6); "until … the morning star rises in your hearts" (2Pe 1:19); "a veil lies over their hearts" (2Co 3:15).; fringe: "I slept, but my heart was awake" (Song 5:2); "Even in the night his heart does not rest" (Ecc 2:23).

17243.text: k. Heart states described through materials [Claude reading on the pattern; the images are the text's]: stone (Eze 11:19; 36:26; Job 41:24; 1Sa 25:37 "his heart died within him, and he became as a stone"); diamond (Zec 7:12); wax, water, melting (Psa 22:14; Jos 7:5; 2Sa 17:10); fat, unfeeling (Psa 119:70); "fattened your hearts" (Jam 5:5); oven (Hos 7:6); deep water (Pro 20:5); a stream of water in God's hand (Pro 21:1); grass struck down and withered (Psa 102:4); burning (Luk 24:32); a mirror: "As in water face reflects face, so the heart of man reflects the man" (Pro 27:19)

17256.text: b. What the soul characteristically does: *Needs and seeks:* thirsts, longs, pants, faints (Psa 107:5; 119:81; Isa 26:8–9), waits (Psa 33:20; 62:1, 5; 130:5–6), hopes (Lam 3:24), clings (Psa 63:8; 119:25 "clings to the dust").; *Suffers:*; bitter (1Sa 1:10; 22:2; 30:6; Job 3:20; 7:11; 10:1; 21:25; 27:2; Isa 38:15; Eze 27:31); cast down, in turmoil (Psa 42:5, 6, 11; 43:5); bowed down (Psa 44:25; 57:6; Lam 3:20); poured out (1Sa 1:15; Job 30:16; Psa 42:4; Isa 53:12 "poured out his soul to death"); refuses comfort (Psa 77:2); is troubled (Psa 6:3; Joh 12:27); "very sorrowful, even to death" (Mat 26:38; Mar 14:34); "my soul is bereft of peace; I have forgotten what happiness is" (Lam 3:17); "vexed to death" (Judg 16:16); *Responds with joy and worship:* rejoices and exults (Isa 61:10; Psa 35:9); boasts in the Lord (Psa 34:2); blesses the Lord (Psa 103:1–2, 22; 104:1, 35; 146:1); "My soul magnifies the Lord" (Luk 1:46); keeps testimonies (Psa 119:129, 167); knows (Psa 139:14).; *Loves and hates:* "the soul of Jonathan was knit to the soul of David" (1Sa 18:1); "his soul hates the wicked" (Psa 11:5); "soul abhors" (Lev 26:15, 43); "malice of soul" (Eze 25:6, 15).; *Is satisfied or not:* Psa 63:5; 107:9; Jer 31:14, 25; Ecc 6:3; Pro 13:4.; *Is lifted up:* "To you, O Lord, I lift up my soul" (Psa 25:1; 86:4; 143:8); contrast "who does not lift up his soul to what is false" (Psa 24:4).; *Is addressed by its owner* — fringe, but many verses: "Why are you cast down, O my soul?" (Psa 42:5, 11; 43:5); "Bless the Lord, O my soul" (Psa 103:1); "Return, O my soul, to your rest" (Psa 116:7); "For God alone, O my soul, wait in silence" (Psa 62:5); "I have calmed and quieted my soul" (Psa 131:2); "March on, my soul, with might!" (Judg 5:21); The rich fool: "I will say to my soul, 'Soul, … relax, eat, drink, be merry'" (Luk 12:19); [Claude reading] The soul is something a person can stand beside, speak to, quiet and command. There is an "I" that addresses "my soul".

17259.text: a. One word: wind, breath, spirit, Spirit, spirits, side, temper: *Wind:* storms, the east wind, the four winds (e.g. Exo 14:21; 1Ki 19:11; Jon 1:4; Psa 1:4).; *Breath:* "the breath of life" (Gen 7:22); "put breath in you, and you shall live" (Eze 37:5–10).; *A person's spirit:* troubled, revived, broken, lowly (below).; *God's Spirit:* rushing upon, filling, indwelling (below).; *Other spirits:* lying (1Ki 22:21–23), harmful (1Sa 16:14–23), unclean (Mar 1–9; Luk 4–11), deceitful (1Ti 4:1).; *"Side" of the compass* (H7307I; 1Ch 9:24; Eze 42:16–20) — fringe: *wind* = *direction*.; *Temper* (H7307J): "hasty temper" (Pro 14:29); "cool spirit" (Pro 17:27); "A fool gives full vent to his spirit" (Pro 29:11); "A man without self-control is like a city broken into and left without walls" (Pro 25:28) — fringe: self-control = governing one's *rûaḥ*; lacking it = a city without walls.; fringe: "the Lord God walking in the garden in the cool [rûaḥ] of the day" (Gen 3:8).

17260.text: b. The human spirit: *Troubled, anxious:* Gen 41:8; Dan 2:1, 3; 7:15 ("my spirit within me was anxious, and the visions of my head alarmed me"); Joh 13:21; 2Co 2:13.; *Revived:*; after eating ("his spirit revived" 1Sa 30:12); after drinking ("his spirit returned, and he revived" Judg 15:19); on good news (Gen 45:27); *Broken, crushed:* Exo 6:9 ("broken spirit and harsh slavery"); Pro 15:4, 13; 17:22; 18:14 ("A man's spirit will endure sickness, but a crushed spirit who can bear?"); Job 17:1; Psa 34:18; 51:17.; *Faint, failing:* Psa 77:3; 142:3; 143:4, 7; Isa 57:16; 61:3.; *Lowly, contrite vs proud, haughty:* Isa 57:15; 66:2; Pro 16:18–19; 29:23; Ecc 7:8; Mat 5:3 ("poor in spirit").; *Governed or ungoverned:* "he who rules his spirit than he who takes a city" (Pro 16:32); "Be not quick in your spirit to become angry" (Ecc 7:9).; *Weighed by God:* "the Lord weighs the spirit" (Pro 16:2).; *Knowing and understanding:*; "it is the spirit in man, the breath of the Almighty, that makes him understand" (Job 32:8); "out of my understanding a spirit answers me" (Job 20:3); "the spirit within me constrains me" (Job 32:18); "who knows a person's thoughts except the spirit of that person, which is in him?" (1Co 2:11) — [Claude reading] the spirit as the person's self-knowledge.; *Distinct from "mind" (nous) in prayer:* "my spirit prays but my mind is unfruitful … I will pray with my spirit, but I will pray with my mind also" (1Co 14:14–15); "be renewed in the spirit of your minds" (Eph 4:23).; *Jesus' spirit:* "perceiving in his spirit" (Mar 2:8); "sighed deeply in his spirit" (Mar 8:12); "deeply moved in his spirit" (Joh 11:33); "troubled in his spirit" (Joh 13:21); "yielded up his spirit" (Mat 27:50; Joh 19:30; Luk 23:46).; *Paul's spirit:* "his spirit was provoked within him" (Act 17:16); "my spirit was not at rest" (2Co 2:13); "refreshed my spirit" (1Co 16:18); "I serve with my spirit" (Rom 1:9).; *Fervent:* "fervent in spirit" (Rom 12:11; Act 18:25); "grew and became strong in spirit" (Luk 1:80).; *Stirred by God:*; "the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus" (2Ch 36:22; Ezr 1:1); "everyone whose spirit God had stirred" (Ezr 1:5); the spirit of Zerubbabel (Hag 1:14); of Pul (1Ch 5:26); of the Medes (Jer 51:11); *Hardened by God:* "the Lord your God hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate" (Deu 2:30).

17263.text: d. God's Spirit acting on and in the inner seat: *Comes upon, rushes upon, clothes:* Judg 3:10; 6:34; 14:6, 19; 15:14; 1Sa 10:6, 10 ("be turned into another man"); 16:13; 1Ch 12:18; 2Ch 24:20.; *Fills with ability:* "filled him with the Spirit of God, with ability and intelligence, with knowledge and all craftsmanship" (Exo 31:3; 35:31).; *Enters and sets on feet:* Eze 2:2; 3:24.; *Put within → changed conduct:* "I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes" (Eze 36:27; 37:14).; *Dwells in:* Rom 8:9, 11; 1Co 3:16; "your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you" (1Co 6:19); 2Ti 1:14; Jam 4:5 ("the spirit that he has made to dwell in us").; *Bears witness with our spirit:* Rom 8:16.; *Placed in the heart:* "given his Spirit in our hearts" (2Co 1:22); "sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, 'Abba! Father!'" (Gal 4:6).; *Pours love into hearts:* Rom 5:5.; *Writes on hearts:* 2Co 3:3.; *Strengthens the inner being:* Eph 3:16.; *Intercedes:* Rom 8:26–27 ("he who searches hearts knows what is the mind of the Spirit").; *Can be grieved, resisted, lied to, quenched:* Isa 63:10; Eph 4:30; Act 7:51 ("uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit"); Act 5:3; 1Th 5:19.; *Can depart or be taken:* 1Sa 16:14; Psa 51:11.; *In the nostrils / made me:* "as long as my breath is in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils" (Job 27:3); "The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life" (Job 33:4).; *Formed within:* "who … formed the spirit of man within him" (Zec 12:1); "gives breath to the people … and spirit to those who walk in it" (Isa 42:5).

17264.text: e. Wind and breath in relation to the inner being — explicitly retained per the researcher: *Breath = life in flesh:*; "all flesh in which is the breath of life" (Gen 6:17; 7:15, 22); "sinews … flesh … skin … But there was no breath in them" → "breath came into them, and they lived" (Eze 37:6–10); "When you take away their breath, they die and return to their dust" (Psa 104:29); *Breath and thought:* "When his breath departs, he returns to the earth; on that very day his plans perish" (Psa 146:4). Link to the thought vocabulary (see brief §5).; *Breath as frailty:* "Remember that my life is a breath" (Job 7:7); "They all have the same breath, and man has no advantage over the beasts" (Ecc 3:19); "He remembered that they were but flesh, a wind that passes and comes not again" (Psa 78:39).; *No breath = no inner life:* idols have "no breath in them" (Jer 10:14; 51:17; Hab 2:19; Psa 135:17). fringe: "there was no more breath in her" = the queen of Sheba overwhelmed (1Ki 10:5; 2Ch 9:4).; *Wind as the emptiness of inner striving* (Ecclesiastes): "I applied my heart to know wisdom … this also is but a striving after wind" (Ecc 1:17); the same in 1:14; 2:11, 17, 26; 4:4, 6, 16; 5:16; "Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the appetite: this also is vanity and a striving after wind" (Ecc 6:9) — appetite (nephesh) + wind; *Wind as empty words:*; "windy knowledge … fill his belly with the east wind" (Job 15:2); "windy words" (Job 16:3); "the speech of a despairing man is wind" (Job 6:26); "the words of your mouth be a great wind" (Job 8:2); "The prophets will become wind; the word is not in them" (Jer 5:13); "utter wind and lies" (Mic 2:11); *Wind as empty outcome:* "we have given birth to wind" (Isa 26:18); "Whoever troubles his own household will inherit the wind" (Pro 11:29); "sow the wind, and … reap the whirlwind" (Hos 8:7); "Ephraim feeds on the wind" (Hos 12:1).; *Wind as the image for a shaken heart:* "the heart of Ahaz and the heart of his people shook as the trees of the forest shake before the wind" (Isa 7:2).; *Wind and lust:* "a wild donkey … in her heat sniffing the wind! Who can restrain her lust?" (Jer 2:24); "to restrain her is to restrain the wind" (Pro 27:16).

17266.text: a. Hebrew flesh: the whole visible, related, mortal person: *Body and meat:* the purity law (Lev 13–16), sacrifices, "meat" in the wilderness (Num 11) and in cooking.; *Kin:*; "we are your bone and flesh" (2Sa 5:1; Gen 29:14); "he is our brother, our own flesh" (Gen 37:27); "not to hide yourself from your own flesh" (Isa 58:7); "close relative" (Lev 18:6; 25:49, H7607); "one flesh" (Gen 2:24; Mat 19:5–6; Mar 10:8; Eph 5:31); *"All flesh" = every living being / humankind:* Gen 6:12–13; Isa 40:5–6 ("All flesh is grass"); Jer 32:27 ("the God of all flesh"); "the God of the spirits of all flesh" (Num 16:22; 27:16).; *Frailty in contrast to God:*; "What can flesh do to me?" (Psa 56:4); "an arm of flesh" (2Ch 32:8); "Cursed is the man who trusts in man and makes flesh his strength, whose heart turns away from the Lord" (Jer 17:5); "their horses are flesh, and not spirit" (Isa 31:3); "My Spirit shall not abide in man forever, for he is flesh" (Gen 6:3); *Flesh responding to the inner seat:*; "My flesh trembles for fear of you" (Psa 119:120); "shuddering seizes my flesh" (Job 21:6); "the hair of my flesh stood up" when a spirit glided past (Job 4:15) — spirit → flesh; "my soul thirsts for you; my flesh faints for you" (Psa 63:1); "my heart and flesh sing for joy" (Psa 84:2); "my heart is glad … my flesh also dwells secure" (Psa 16:9; Act 2:26); "My flesh and my heart may fail" (Psa 73:26); "A tranquil heart gives life to the flesh" (Pro 14:30); "they are life to those who find them, and healing to all their flesh" (Pro 4:22); "There is no soundness in my flesh because of your indignation; there is no health in my bones because of my sin" (Psa 38:3); "much study is a weariness of the flesh" (Ecc 12:12); "Ahab … put sackcloth on his flesh" (1Ki 21:27); *Heart of flesh vs heart of stone:* "I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh" (Eze 11:19; 36:26). Here *flesh* is the good state of the heart: responsive, living.; *Life is in the blood of the flesh:* "the life of the flesh is in the blood" (Lev 17:11, 14; Gen 9:4; Deu 12:23).

17267.text: b. Greek *sarx*: *Neutral uses continue:* one flesh; all flesh; "the Word became flesh" (Joh 1:14); "in the days of his flesh" (Heb 5:7); "flesh and blood" (Heb 2:14; Mat 16:17); "a thorn … in the flesh" (2Co 12:7); "our bodies had no rest … fighting without and fear within" (2Co 7:5).; *Pauline and Petrine ethical flesh — flesh as an inner orientation:*; "the desires of the flesh and the desires of the eyes" (1Jo 2:16); "the passions of our flesh, carrying out the desires of the flesh and the mind" (Eph 2:3); "the works of the flesh" (Gal 5:19); "crucified the flesh with its passions and desires" (Gal 5:24); "nothing good dwells in me, that is, in my flesh. For I have the desire to do what is right, but not the ability to carry it out" (Rom 7:18); "I myself serve the law of God with my mind, but with my flesh I serve the law of sin" (Rom 7:25); "the mind that is set on the flesh is hostile to God" (Rom 8:7); "sensuous mind" = mind of the flesh (Col 2:18) [lexical]; "confidence in the flesh" (Phili 3:3–4); "boast according to the flesh" (2Co 11:18); "judge according to the flesh" (Joh 8:15); "regard no one according to the flesh" (2Co 5:16); "plans according to the flesh" (2Co 1:17); [Claude reading] Flesh here is no longer just the body. It is a way the inner person is *oriented*, with its own desires and "mind".

17268.text: 2.5 Conscience — *syneidēsis* (G4893, NT only): *Bears witness:* "their conscience also bears witness, and their conflicting thoughts accuse or even excuse them" (Rom 2:15); "my conscience bears me witness in the Holy Spirit" (Rom 9:1); "the testimony of our conscience" (2Co 1:12).; *Good, clear:* Act 23:1; 24:16; 1Ti 1:5, 19; 3:9; 2Ti 1:3; Heb 13:18; 1Pe 3:16.; *Weak, defiled, wounded:* 1Co 8:7, 10, 12. *Seared:* 1Ti 4:2. *Evil:* Heb 10:22.; *Defiled together with the mind:* "both their minds and their consciences are defiled" (Tit 1:15).; *Purified:* "the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself … [will] purify our conscience from dead works" (Heb 9:14); gifts and sacrifices "cannot perfect the conscience" (Heb 9:9); "consciousness of sins" (Heb 10:2).; *Other people's conscience:* "not your conscience, but his" (1Co 10:29); "commend ourselves to everyone's conscience" (2Co 4:2); "known also to your conscience" (2Co 5:11); "for the sake of conscience" (Rom 13:5; 1Co 10:25–28).; *Baptism as "an appeal to God for a good conscience"*, not removal of dirt from the body (1Pe 3:21).; fringe: "mindful of God" (1Pe 2:19) and "consciousness" (Heb 10:2) are tagged G4893. The word covers *awareness* as well as moral judgment [Claude reading].

17269.text: 2.6 Bosom / embrace — *ḥêq* (H2436G) ◆ mostly fringe, but relevant: *Holding loved ones:* in her arms, at her breast, on her lap (1Ki 3:20; 17:19; Rut 4:16); "carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries a nursing child" (Num 11:12); "he will carry them in his bosom" (Isa 40:11); "the wife you embrace" (Deu 13:6; 28:54, 56).; *As an inner seat:*; "anger lodges in the heart [bosom] of fools" (Ecc 7:9); "how I bear in my heart [bosom] the insults of all the many nations" (Psa 89:50); "My heart faints within me!" (Job 19:27; tagged on "within"); "I prayed with head bowed on my chest" (Psa 35:13); *Life poured out on the bosom:* "their life is poured out on their mothers' bosom" (Lam 2:12).; [Claude reading] The bosom is where one holds *others* and where one holds *feelings* (anger, insults). The same place carries both.

17272.text: 3.2 Totality and wholeness formulas: *Heart and soul (and might):*; "with all your heart and with all your soul (and with all your might)" (Deu 4:29; 6:5; 10:12; 11:13; 13:3; 26:16; 30:2, 6, 10; Jos 22:5; 1Ki 2:4; 8:48; 2Ki 23:3, 25; 2Ch 6:38; 15:12; 34:31; Jer 32:41 — said of God); "you know in your hearts and souls" (Jos 23:14); "lay up these words … in your heart and in your soul" (Deu 11:18); "keep your soul diligently, lest … they depart from your heart" (Deu 4:9); "I am with you heart and soul" (1Sa 14:7, ESV idiom; only *lēvāv* is tagged); "one heart and soul" (Act 4:32); *NT expansion — heart, soul, mind, strength:* Mat 22:37; Mar 12:30; Luk 10:27; "heart … understanding … strength" (Mar 12:33).; *Whole person with an outer term added:*; "spirit and soul and body" (1Th 5:23); "soul and body" (Isa 10:18; Mat 10:28; Psa 31:9; Pro 16:24); "heart and flesh" (Psa 73:26; 84:2; Eze 44:7, 9); "body and spirit" (1Co 7:34; 2Co 7:1); "vexation from your heart … pain from your body" (Ecc 11:10); [Claude reading] Wholeness is expressed by *adding* terms, not by defining parts. The pairs work as merisms: the whole person seen from two or three sides at once.

17276.text: 3.6 Cause and effect between inner seat, body and senses: *Heart → spirit:* "by sorrow of heart the spirit is crushed" (Pro 15:13).; *Heart / spirit → body, face, bones:*; "A glad heart makes a cheerful face" (Pro 15:13); "A tranquil heart gives life to the flesh, but envy makes the bones rot" (Pro 14:30); "A joyful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones" (Pro 17:22); "a trembling heart and failing eyes and a languishing soul" (Deu 28:65); "My heart throbs; my strength fails me, and the light of my eyes — it also has gone" (Psa 38:10); "Every heart will melt, and all hands will be feeble; every spirit will faint, and all knees will be weak as water" (Eze 21:7); "Hearts melt and knees tremble; anguish is in all loins; all faces grow pale" (Nah 2:10); "My heart is struck down like grass … I forget to eat my bread" (Psa 102:4); "My heart is broken within me; all my bones shake" (Jer 23:9); "your heart shall rejoice; your bones shall flourish like the grass" (Isa 66:14); "For this our heart has become sick, for these things our eyes have grown dim" (Lam 5:17); "my stomach churns; my heart is wrung within me" (Lam 1:20); *Body / face / senses → heart:*; "by sadness of face the heart is made glad" (Ecc 7:3); "The light of the eyes rejoices the heart, and good news refreshes the bones" (Pro 15:30); "my heart has gone after my eyes" (Job 31:7); "not to follow after your own heart and your own eyes" (Num 15:39); "everyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart" (Mat 5:28); *Food and drink → heart / spirit / soul:*; "Strengthen your heart with a morsel of bread" (Judg 19:5, 8); "wine to gladden the heart of man … bread to strengthen man's heart" (Psa 104:15); "satisfying your hearts with food and gladness" (Act 14:17); "when he had eaten, his spirit revived" (1Sa 30:12); "when he drank, his spirit returned" (Judg 15:19); "when the wine had gone out of Nabal … his heart died within him, and he became as a stone" (1Sa 25:37); "it is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace, not by foods" (Heb 13:9); "Oil and perfume make the heart glad" (Pro 27:9); *Fasting afflicts the soul:* Psa 35:13 ("I afflicted myself [nephesh] with fasting"); Psa 69:10; Isa 58:3, 5; the Day of Atonement "afflict yourselves" (Lev 16:29–31; 23:27–32; Num 29:7).

17277.text: 3.6 Cause and effect between inner seat, body and senses: *Appetite (soul) and heart:* "They tested God in their heart by demanding the food they craved" (Psa 78:18); the fool's heart "busy with iniquity … to leave the craving of the hungry unsatisfied" (Isa 32:6); "you crave meat" (Deu 12:20).; *Heart → mouth, hands, feet, deeds:* §2.1h. Also: "clean hands and a pure heart" (Psa 24:4); "Let us lift up our hearts and hands to God" (Lam 3:41); "a heart that devises wicked plans, feet that make haste to run to evil" (Pro 6:18); "The heart of man plans his way, but the Lord establishes his steps" (Pro 16:9); "The law of his God is in his heart; his steps do not slip" (Psa 37:31); *Heart ↔ ears / hearing* — link to the brief's hearing question: "hear with their ears, and understand with their hearts" (Isa 6:10; Mat 13:15; Act 28:27); "making your ear attentive to wisdom and inclining your heart to understanding" (Pro 2:2); "Incline your ear … apply your heart" (Pro 22:17; 23:12); "receive in your heart, and hear with your ears" (Eze 3:10); "hear with your ears … set your heart upon all that I shall show you" (Eze 40:4); "uncircumcised in heart and ears" (Act 7:51); "The Lord opened her heart to pay attention" (Act 16:14); "They made their hearts diamond-hard lest they should hear the law" (Zec 7:12); "Incline your ear, and come to me; hear, that your soul may live" (Isa 55:3) — soul + hearing; "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts" (Heb 3:7–8, 15; 4:7; Psa 95:8); [Claude reading] Hearing and heart are joined repeatedly: the ear receives, the heart understands or refuses. Hardness of heart and failure to hear go together.

17278.text: 3.7 Containment — what is placed "in" what: *In the heart:*; law, words, commandments (Deu 6:6; Psa 37:31; 119:11; Jer 31:33); wisdom (Pro 2:10; 14:33); fear of God (Jer 32:40); eternity (Ecc 3:11); idols (Eze 14:3); deceit (Pro 12:20); folly (Pro 22:15); anger (Ecc 7:9); the Spirit (2Co 1:22; Gal 4:6); Christ "may dwell in your hearts through faith" (Eph 3:17); "the peace of Christ rule in your hearts" (Col 3:15); "the word of Christ dwell in you richly … thankfulness in your hearts" (Col 3:16); God's love "poured into our hearts" (Rom 5:5); what "the devil had already put into the heart of Judas" (Joh 13:2); what "God has put into their hearts" (Rev 17:17; Neh 2:12; 7:5; Ezr 7:27; 2Co 8:16); *Within me:* spirit (Psa 143:4; Isa 26:9; Job 32:18; Dan 7:15); soul (Psa 42:5–6; 131:2); heart (Psa 22:14; 39:3; 109:22; Jer 8:18; 23:9; Lam 1:20; Hos 11:8).; *Spirit and heart inside flesh:* "I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh" (Eze 36:26); "put breath in you" (Eze 37:6).; *Spirit and body:* "your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you" (1Co 6:19); "if the Spirit … dwells in you, he … will also give life to your mortal bodies" (Rom 8:11).; [Claude reading] The heart is the innermost *location* in the text's picture. Soul-states, spirit, God's Spirit, words, law and dispositions are placed "in" it. Spirit and soul are also spoken of as "within me", but they are less often described as containers.

17281.text: 3.10 God, animals and things — the vocabulary is not limited to humans ◆ fringe: *God has a heart:* grieved (Gen 6:6); speaks in it (Gen 8:21); "a man after my own heart" (1Sa 13:14; Act 13:22); "My heart recoils within me; my compassion grows warm and tender" (Hos 11:8); "he does not afflict from his heart" (Lam 3:33); "my eyes and my heart will be there" (1Ki 9:3); "the intents of his heart" (Jer 23:20); "with all my heart and all my soul" (Jer 32:41).; *God has a soul:* "my soul hates" (Isa 1:14); "my soul delights" (Isa 42:1; Mat 12:18); "my soul shall not abhor you" (Lev 26:11); "Does your soul loathe Zion?" (Jer 14:19); "my soul has no pleasure in him" (Heb 10:38); "The Lord God has sworn by himself [nephesh]" (Amo 6:8; Jer 51:14); "shall I not avenge myself [nephesh]" (Jer 5:9, 29; 9:9).; *God's spirit and breath:* "the breath of his mouth" (Psa 33:6); "the breath of his lips" (Isa 11:4); "God is spirit" (Joh 4:24).; *Animals:*; "living creatures" (nephesh, Gen 1); "They all have the same breath" (Ecc 3:19); "the spirit of the beast" (Ecc 3:21); a beast's mind given to a man (Dan 4:16); "the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels" (Eze 1:20–21; 10:17); "all flesh" includes animals (Gen 6–9); *Places and things:* heart of the sea, earth and heaven (§2.1a); Sheol's appetite (Isa 5:14); idols with no breath (§2.3e).

17282.text: 4. Fringe observations collected (quick list): Heart = "midst" of sea, heaven, earth; the inner seat named as the *middle* (§2.1a).; Aaron carries the tribes "on his heart" before the Lord (Exo 28:29–30).; "I slept, but my heart was awake" (Song 5:2).; "Eyes of your hearts" (Eph 1:18); morning star rising in hearts (2Pe 1:19); a veil over hearts (2Co 3:15).; "Walls of my heart" (Jer 4:19); "tear open their breast" (Hos 13:8); a man without self-control = "a city … without walls" (Pro 25:28, rûaḥ). The inner seat is imaged as an enclosure.; Nabal's heart "died within him, and he became as a stone" after the wine left (1Sa 25:37).; Nephesh = neck/throat (Psa 69:1; 105:18) and = corpse (Num 19:11).; Knife to the throat "if you are given to appetite" (Pro 23:2).; Sheol's "appetite" and "mouth" (Isa 5:14).; "Perfume boxes" tagged nephesh (Isa 3:20).; A millstone in pledge = "a life in pledge" (Deu 24:6).; The soul addressed by its owner (Psa 42; 103; 116:7; 131:2; Luk 12:19).; rûaḥ = compass *side* (1Ch 9:24; Eze 42:16–20).; rûaḥ = "cool" of the day when God walked in the garden (Gen 3:8).; Dispositions as "spirits" that come upon a person: jealousy, whoredom, confusion, deep sleep, stupor, skill, grace (§2.3c).; Spirits causing muteness or a bent back (Mar 9:17; Luk 13:11).; "A spirit glided past my face; the hair of my flesh stood up" (Job 4:15).; "Present in spirit" though absent in body (1Co 5:3; Col 2:5).; Spirit of Elijah on Elisha; Moses' Spirit shared with the elders (2Ki 2; Num 11).; Queen of Sheba: "there was no more breath in her" (1Ki 10:5).; Man's heart/mind exchanged for a beast's (Dan 4:16; 5:21; 7:4).; "The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares its joy" (Pro 14:10) — the privacy of the inner seat.; "As in water face reflects face, so the heart of man reflects the man" (Pro 27:19).; "He has put eternity into man's heart" (Ecc 3:11).; Spirit-birth pictured by the wind (Joh 3:8).; Plans perish when the breath departs (Psa 146:4) — breath and thought.; Bread strengthens the heart (Judg 19:5; Psa 104:15), yet food "enters not his heart but his stomach" (Mar 7:19), and the heart should be strengthened "by grace, not by foods" (Heb 13:9). Three verses, three angles on the same relation.; The bosom holds both loved ones and anger or insults (Ecc 7:9; Psa 89:50).; "Conscience" also = "consciousness / mindful" (Heb 10:2; 1Pe 2:19).

17283.text: 4. Fringe observations collected (quick list): God's own heart and soul (§3.10).

17288.text: 3. Why they were not narrated: The anger units read the anger words. The M18 side of these verses was jealousy, delight, favour, desire, or willing, and it was left. In most cases it is God's jealousy beside his wrath. The anger ledger has it (AG-04, AG-73–76), but 10.13 carries it as one "joined with" bullet (Deu 6:15). There was no account of God's jealousy until 13.1 *Jealousy* was opened earlier today from the held items.; One verse, Job 6:2, is listed in the anger ledger as already in the chapters. A text search finds it nowhere, and it is now woven.

17291.text: 10.7 *Choosing and setting direction* | v20 | Mat 19 (and the Isaiah 1 "one place" sentence restated); Joh 5:40–44; Ruth 3:10–13, 4:4–6; 2Ti 3:11–12; Joh 21:18–22; 2Ch 19:2–3; Pro 14:13–14; Dan 11:25; Isa 47:13–14

17295.text: 10.10 *Relating to others* | v15 | 1Sa 19:1–7 in *Loyalty and honour*; Deu 19:6 in *Anger between people*; new *Friends, company and care* (Job 6:15–18; Ecc 4:9–11; Job 31:19–20; Job 17:8–9 against 31:29–30; Pro 10:12; Song 2:7)

17307.text: 3. (a) Why the verses were not narrated: There is one main reason. The M47 reset narrated the seat words (heart, soul, spirit, flesh) and left the desire side of each verse to a later strand. This is that strand. So 10.6 *Wanting* was short (38 lines). It had nothing on: desire in the heart through the eye (Mat 5:28; Pro 6:25); delight and its objects (Psa 119:70; Isa 55:2; Pro 18:2; Psa 40:14); the wilderness craving (Num 11); evil desire (Pro 21:10; Psa 10:3; Mic 7:3); longing for people (1Th 2:17; Rom 1:11); what is desired being taken away (Eze 24:21, 25); Ch 5 had no account of a life held precious (1Sa 26:21; 2Ki 1:13–14; Pro 6:26; Psa 49:7–8).; Two smaller reasons:

17314.text: 5. (c) Errors realigned: Ch 5, "exhaustion". Ch 5 v3 called Job 10:1, Ecc 2:17 and Jon 4:3 "a third kind of hating one's life, which is exhaustion rather than discipleship". The verses give their own ground: Job: bitterness of soul; the Preacher: "what is done under the sun was grievous to me"; Jonah: anger that God spared Nineveh (4:1–4); faintness comes only with the second wish (4:8); The frame came from M47 batch G §6. Ch 5 now gives each ground. Ch 2 already read Jonah correctly.; Ch 4, Pro 21:1. It was listed among the "materials" for the state a heart is in. It is a heart being directed, "wherever he will", and "will" is the delight word. It is now set apart in Ch 4 and placed in 13.1 *Delight*.

17318.text: 2. Scale: For comparison, M64 had 28 Strong's, 493 hits and 468 verses. M18 is about three times its size.; Books with the most M18 verses: Psa 139, Pro 108, Isa 70, Mat 59, Ecc 52, Gen 46, Deu 45, Luk 43, 1Sa 42, 1Ki 41, Joh 37, Eze 36, Rom 33, 2Ch 32.

17324.text: 2.1 Bucket 3 (269): *ṭôb* said of things, people and acts: These need to come out of bucket 3 before anything is parked. The rule could not separate them because the paired word, LORD or God, carries a T-code.; Examples: Deu 4:21 "the good land"; 2Sa 18:27 "He is a good man"; Pro 15:17 "Better is a dinner of herbs where love is than a fattened ox and hatred with it"; Gen 41:22 "seven ears … full and good"

17326.text: 2.3 Bucket 1 (254): inner-being candidates: Examples: Jer 40:4 "If it seems good to you to come with me to Babylon"; Est 5:9 "joyful and glad of heart"; Mat 3:17 "with whom I am well pleased" (God's own pleasure: route A)

17473.text: His keeping. *"A pleasant vineyard, sing of it! I, the Lord, am its keeper; every moment I water it … I have no wrath"* (Isa 27:2–4).

17515.text: Passage: the friends say *"God stores up their iniquity for their children"* (21:19). Job answers, *"Let him pay it out to them, that they may know it. Let their own eyes see their destruction"* (21:19–20).

17532.text: Reading: in a psalm of how short a man's life is (90:3–10, 12), the last request is that something of their own work should last. It is asked through his favor resting on them, set beside "your work" (90:16).

17581.text: Reading: what Balaam had worked against twice (Num 22–23), he now sees. Once he knows what pleases the Lord, he stops seeking omens and sets his face in a direction.

17633.text: Scorned word: "the word of the Lord is to them an object of scorn; they take no pleasure in it", with ears that "cannot listen" (Jer 6:10). The prophet is set beside them: "I am full of the wrath of the Lord; I am weary of holding it in" (6:11). This also goes to 10.2.

17751.text: God's own, in a man | 2Co 11:2–3 (with Num 25:11) | Paul's "divine jealousy", a husband's jealousy for the bridegroom, joined to fear for their thoughts

17760.text: 3. A husband's jealousy with no witness (10.6): Num 5:14–31. The "spirit of jealousy" comes over the husband whether the wife "has defiled herself" or "has not" (5:14): the law itself says the jealousy may be wrong. The offering is "of jealousy … of remembrance", with no oil and no frankincense (5:15). The matter is not his to settle: "he shall set the woman before the Lord" (5:30); "The man shall be free from iniquity" (5:31). Beside Pro 6:34–35, where a husband's jealousy "will accept no compensation", I read the law as taking the jealousy out of the husband's hands and putting it before God. Num 5:18 and 5:25 (the ritual) are carried by this account.

17763.text: For Zion: the answer to an angel's "how long" | Zec 1:12–16 | Jealous for her, angry at the nations who "furthered the disaster" beyond his "little" anger, returned "with mercy"

17767.text: The same fire in the New Testament | Heb 10:26–27 | "a fury [zeal] of fire that will consume the adversaries"

17779.text: Met, then forgotten: Neh 9:15–17 ("acted presumptuously … not mindful of the wonders"); Isa 48:21–22. I read a want met so fully that it was no longer felt, and the giver forgotten with it (10.3).

17840.text: It answers a bond given to another.; *"They stirred him to jealousy with strange gods; with abominations they provoked him to anger"* (Deu 32:16). Before it: *"Jeshurun grew fat, and kicked; you grew fat, stout, and sleek; then he forsook God who made him"* (32:15). After it: *"You were unmindful of the Rock that bore you"* (32:18).; *"they moved him to jealousy with their idols"* (Psa 78:58).; I read: jealousy in God is roused where the bond he made is given to another. The verses name a fullness that kicked, and a forgetting.

17841.text: It is answered in kind. *"They have made me jealous with what is no god … So I will make them jealous with those who are no people"* (Deu 32:21). The measure of the answer is the offence itself, "no god" for "no people". Paul takes it up (Rom 10:19, in the anger ledger AG-217).

17842.text: Against his own, as against an unfaithful wife.; *"I will judge you as women who commit adultery and shed blood are judged, and bring upon you the blood of wrath and jealousy"* (Eze 16:38).; *"I will direct my jealousy against you, that they may deal with you in fury"* (23:25). It is carried by *"your lovers"*, the ones she desired (23:22, 10.6, 13.1 *Stirring*).

17843.text: Against one man who blesses himself. *"the anger of the Lord and his jealousy will smoke against that man"* (Deu 29:20). He is the one who *"blesses himself in his heart, saying, 'I shall be safe'"* (29:19). The inner act of self-assurance is what the jealousy smokes against. (13.1 *Willing* already has 29:20 for "not willing to forgive".)

17844.text: For Zion. *"I am jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and I am jealous for her with great wrath"* (Zec 8:2). The next verse is *"I have returned to Zion and will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem"* (8:3). The jealousy for her ends in his dwelling with her.

17845.text: Over the whole earth, and then a pure speech. *"in the fire of my jealousy all the earth shall be consumed"* (Zep 3:8). Then: *"For at that time I will change the speech of the peoples to a pure speech, that all of them may call upon the name of the Lord"* (3:9). The passage puts the fire and the pure speech side by side. In Zep 1:18, *"Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them … In the fire of his jealousy, all the earth shall be consumed"*.

17846.text: Creation shaken. *"For in my jealousy and in my blazing wrath I declare, On that day there shall be a great earthquake … all the people who are on the face of the earth, shall quake at my presence"* (Eze 38:19–20).

17847.text: Jealous, and slow to anger, side by side. *"The Lord is a jealous and avenging God … and keeps wrath for his enemies. The Lord is slow to anger and great in power"* (Nah 1:2–3). The verses put both in one breath. I do not reconcile them.

17848.text: It ends, and something follows.; *"So will I satisfy my wrath on you, and my jealousy shall depart from you. I will be calm and will no more be angry"* (Eze 16:42). The next verse names what had enraged him: *"Because you have not remembered the days of your youth"* (16:43).; *"And they shall know that I am the Lord—that I have spoken in my jealousy"* (Eze 5:13). The stated end is knowing.

17849.text: Asked about in lament. *"How long, O Lord? Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy burn like fire? Pour out your anger on the nations that do not know you"* (Psa 79:5–6). I read a people asking for the jealousy to end on them and to turn on others. The ledger reads the same (AG-88).

17851.text: 2. A person who shares God's jealousy (10.6 *Jealousy and envy*): *"Phinehas … has turned back my wrath from the people of Israel, in that he was jealous with my jealousy among them"*. He is given *"my covenant of peace"*, *"because he was jealous for his God and made atonement for the people of Israel"* (Num 25:11–13). 10.9 has it.

17855.text: Not envy. *"The wicked man sees it and is angry; he gnashes his teeth and melts away; the desire of the wicked will perish!"* (Psa 112:10). What he sees is the righteous man's honour (112:9). The anger ledger records that no verse names envy here (F.6). So it goes under *Evil desire*: where the desire of the wicked ends.

17857.text: 5. Where a desire ends (10.6 *Evil desire*): *"The desire of the righteous ends only in good, the expectation of the wicked in wrath"* (Pro 11:23). With Psa 112:10, "the desire of the wicked will perish!". I read the proverbs judging a desire by where it ends.

17858.text: 6. What is desired, taken by God (10.6 *Taken away*): *"He has bent his bow like an enemy … and he has killed all who were delightful in our eyes"* (Lam 2:4). *"The Lord has become like an enemy"* (2:5).

17860.text: 7. Whose measure (10.7 *Whose measure*): *"But Naaman was angry and went away, saying, 'Behold, I thought that he would surely come out to me …' Are not Abana and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel?"* (2Ki 5:11–12).; His own measure ("better") and his own picture of how it should go ("I thought") are set against the prophet's word.; His servants answer with a question: *"My father, it is a great word the prophet has spoken to you; will you not do it? Has he actually said to you, 'Wash, and be clean'?"* (5:13). His *"flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child"* (5:14).

17861.text: The will that stays outside. *"But he was angry and refused to go in. His father came out and entreated him"* (Luk 15:28). The verb is the will word. The older brother's anger takes the form of a will that refuses to go in. The father does not wait inside; he comes out. 10.13 has the anger. 10.7 gets the will.

17862.text: The absolute will with a set end. *"And the king shall do as he wills. He shall exalt himself and magnify himself above every god … He shall prosper till the indignation is accomplished; for what is decreed shall be done"* (Dan 11:36). Compare Nebuchadnezzar, already in 10.7: *"Whom he would, he killed"*, until his heart was lifted up and he was brought down (Dan 5:19–20). In Daniel 11 the absolute will runs until a time already set.

17863.text: God's desire, held in patience. *"What if God, desiring to show his wrath and to make known his power, has endured with much patience vessels of wrath prepared for destruction, in order to make known the riches of his glory for vessels of mercy"* (Rom 9:22–23). Desire, wrath and patience stand in one question, and it is a question ("What if"). 13.1 already has 9:18–20.

17864.text: 9. Favour (13.1 *Delight*; 10.10): *"He does not retain his anger forever, because he delights in steadfast love"* (Mic 7:18). The reason his anger ends is what he delights in.; *"for in my wrath I struck you, but in my favor I have had mercy on you"* (Isa 60:10). Wrath and favour are named in one sentence, with mercy coming from the favour. Compare *"his favor is for a lifetime"* (Psa 30:5, in 10.13).

17865.text: A ruler's favour has a ground. *"A servant who deals wisely has the king's favor, but his wrath falls on one who acts shamefully"* (Pro 14:35), beside *"his favor is like dew on the grass"* (Pro 19:12, in 10.10).

17866.text: 10. Two wishes, and fear (10.10): *"For I fear that perhaps when I come I may find you not as I wish, and that you may find me not as you wish — that perhaps there may be quarreling, jealousy, anger"* (2Co 12:20).; Each side holds a wish about the other.; Paul fears that both will be disappointed, and he names what disappointment would bring.

17868.text: 12. Weight, and rash words (10.5): *"Oh that my vexation were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances! For then it would be heavier than the sand of the sea; therefore my words have been rash"* (Job 6:2–3). Job measures his inner weight and gives it as the reason for his words. Compare Psalm 39, woven today: silence held until the heart burned, then speech turned to God. Here the weight is given as the reason the words came out rash.

17869.text: 13. Error realigned (10.1): 10.1 said *"Grief makes it tender; jealousy makes it hard"* as if the verses said it. They do not say so. Mark 3:5 joins anger with grief. Pro 6:34–35 joins it with jealousy and says the fury refuses every gift. The comparison is mine, so it is restated as a reading.

17910.text: Where: 10.6, the paragraph "Wanting can be aimed at the living God", rewritten around looking (Psa 27), portion (Psa 16) and longing with asking (Psa 119).

17922.text: Where: 10.6, "The thirst is answered" paragraph, rewritten: spring and cistern, the literal ask, and the three answers to thirst. The wilderness craving paragraph (Num 11) gets a pointer to it.

17924.text: Jeremiah 42 in order.: They ask: *"whatever the Lord our God says … we will do it"* (42:20).; God answers with a promise: *"Do not fear the king of Babylon … for I am with you"* (42:11).; They want the opposite: *"No, we will go to the land of Egypt, where we shall not see war or hear the sound of the trumpet or be hungry for bread"* (42:14).; The reply: *"the sword that you fear shall overtake you there … and the famine of which you are afraid shall follow close after you"* (42:16), and *"in the place where you desire to go to live"* (42:22).

17960.text: Compare the two words for Jonathan's bond, and Saul's turn.: 1Sa 18:1, in 10.10: *"the soul of Jonathan was knit to the soul of David"*. That is the bond.; 19:1: "delighted much". That is the bond under threat.; Saul once "rejoiced" at David (19:5). His turn began with a saying that *"displeased him"* and *"Saul eyed David from that day on"* (18:8–9).

18024.text: 7. Data (6): Gen 41:35 (good years), Isa 5:9 (beautiful houses; the woe is 5:8), Est 2:2 and 2:3 (beautiful virgins sought for the king; pointer Est 2:1, 2:4), Est 7:9 ("whose word saved the king"; the passage's act is the king's wrath, 7:7, 10), 1Ki 2:18 (Bathsheba's "Very well"; pointer 1Ki 2:15).

18037.text: Est 1:19. *"If it please the king, let a royal order go out … and let the king give her royal position to another who is better than she."* Memucan's ground is fear of what others will do: the women will *"look at their husbands with contempt"* (1:17), *"and there will be contempt and wrath in plenty"* (1:18). *"This advice pleased the king and the princes"* (1:21).

18066.text: Job 31:16–17: the poor's desire not withheld.: > "If I have withheld anything that the poor desired, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail, or; > have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless has not eaten of it"; These are Job's own words, in the oath God's verdict supports (Job 42:7). Here the M18 word is the; poor man's own desire, which Job swears he did not refuse. "Eaten my morsel alone" names the act of; not sharing. 10.10 already has 31:19–20 from the same oath, and this sits just before it.

18084.text: 1. OT-98.3: the eight verses with an M02 word: All eight are told: Pro 16:32, Zep 3:8, Dan 11:36, Est 5:9, Zec 8:2, Pro 14:35, Isa 60:10, Pro; 19:12. Read outward for what the authority word adds, the tellings carry it: the king's wrath and the king's favour, each with its ground: "A servant who deals wisely has the; king's favor, but his wrath falls on one who acts shamefully" (Pro 14:35; 10.10); "A king's wrath is like the growling of a lion" (Pro 19:12; 10.10, 10.13); ruling one's own spirit (Pro 16:32; Ch 6, 10.13, Ch 11 *Authority as a standing*); Haman's wrath at a man who "neither rose nor trembled before him" (Est 5:9; Ch 4, 10.10, 10.13); the will made absolute (Dan 11:36; 10.7); God's jealousy and wrath (Zep 3:8; Zec 8:2; Isa 60:10; 13.1); OT-16 was closed for M72 under #1998. Proposed: close OT-98.3.

18118.text: For them, against those who scorned them: *"I have spoken in my hot jealousy against the rest of the nations and against all Edom, who gave my land to themselves as a possession with wholehearted joy and utter contempt"* (Eze 36:5). *"I have spoken in my jealous wrath, because you have suffered the reproach of the nations"* (36:6). His jealousy answers someone else's joy at taking what is his.

18122.text: Whose it is: God's, Elijah's, Joshua's, a husband's (Pro 6:34–35, in 10.1), a sister's (Gen 30:1, in 10.6)

Nevertheless, some good is found in you, for you destroyed the Asheroth out of the land, and have set your heart to seek God."* A love wrongly given and a heart set to seek God stand in one king, and the prophet's verdict holds both.

18139.text: Heat that kills (Deu 19:4–6). *"lest the avenger of blood in hot anger pursue the manslayer … though the man did not deserve to die, since he had not hated his neighbor in the past"*. The Hebrew says "while his heart is hot". The law builds cities of refuge because the heat of a grieving relative will not tell the innocent from the guilty. The law allows for the inner state and sets a distance between it and the act ("because the way is long").
